### What happened?

kube-apiserver has has this kind of entries in log
```
E0126 00:39:45.253562       1 fieldmanager.go:210] "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to convert new object (default/test-inline-claim; /v1, Kind=Pod) to smd typed: .spec.containers[name=\"with-resource\"].resources.claims: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" VersionKind="/, Kind=" namespace="default" name="test-inline-claim"

```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected those lines not to appear in kube-apiserver logs, and structured-merge-diff to support map types, like the comment says at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff/v4/typed/helpers.go#L233

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I ran into it during Dynamic Resource Allocation usage. It requires a either a CRI-O v1.23, or containerd 1.7+ (has to be built from git at the moment); the cluster has to be initialized "DynamicResourceAllocation" feature-gate and alpha apis enabled, for instance with this config for kubeadm :
<details>

```YAML

kind: ClusterConfiguration

imageRepository: registry.local

  extraArgs:
    feature-gates: "DynamicResourceAllocation=true"
    runtime-config: "api/alpha=true"

  extraArgs:

  extraArgs:
    "feature-gates": "DynamicResourceAllocation=true"
---

  DynamicResourceAllocation: true
---
apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3
kind: InitConfiguration
nodeRegistration:
  criSocket: "unix:///var/run/crio/crio.sock"
---
apiVersion: kubeproxy.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: KubeProxyConfiguration
featureGates:
  DynamicResourceAllocation: true
```

</details>

Deploy pod with inline resource-claim for instance the following (the issue will appear immediately even though the resource-claim is malformed. Proper resource claim would require resource-driver to be deployed, but it's not necessary for issue to be manifested):
<details>

```YAML

kind: ResourceClaimTemplate
metadata:
  name: test-inline-claim-template
  namespace: default
spec:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: inline-resource
  spec:
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-inline-claim
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: with-resource
    image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/busybox:1.29-2
    command: ["sh", "-c", "ls -la /dev/dri/ && sleep 30"]

      claims:
      - name: resource

      resourceClaimTemplateName: test-inline-claim-template

</details>

Deletecollection failing after 34 seconds
### What happened?

In a cluster with large enough numbers of objects, it seems to be impossible to clean them up with `deletecollection`.  Because the deletecollection is failing while listing the objects from etcd.  The failure happens after exactly 34 seconds, due to the 34-second max timeout introduced in PR #96901 (cc @tkashem for insight on that PR).


### What did you expect to happen?

The deletecollection should be able to run for longer, and succeed.

I recognise that there are still risks of the API server using too much RAM, if deleting a very large collection due to issue #90743.  But, until _that_ issue is fixed, it seems like allowing `deletecollection` to run for longer might be a good idea.  As far as I can tell, the 34 second timeout does not apply to normal LIST calls, so on that basis I feel it should not apply to the giant unchunked LIST call that happens inside `deletecollection`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a few hundred thousand objects of some particular type.  (Argo workflowtaskresults happen to be the type I'm looking at while I write this)
2. Call deletecollection. (Optionally passing some kind of fieldSelector, but I don't think that's essential)
3. Observe that a 504 failure code is logged in kube-audit logs, and that a log entry similar to this is logged by the API Server `"List etcd3" key:<some key>,...,limit:0 ... (total time: 34000ms)`  (In practice, the total time may be a little over 34000 ms).
4. As far as I can tell, the delete collection really has failed at this point.  I notice that PR #96901 says that, in general, "The go-routine can keep running, while the timeout logic will return a timeout to the client" but I don't _think_ that's what's happening here.  I think that, because the 34 sec timeout is used in the context of the etcd call, the etcd list call really does fail, and so the code never proceeds to actually deleting anything.


### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

1.22

kube-apiserver using unregistered and unusual label
### What happened?

The code at
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/86f3fa94f1b75da275a8040e4155840a7b473dc1/pkg/controlplane/instance.go#L126 specifies a ~annotation~ label that API servers set on Leases (each API server registers its own lease).

https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/architecture/leases/#api-server-identity is likely to document this once v1.26 is released; the alpha for API server identity didn't get documented.

Here's the problems:
- as a project, we use `kubernetes.io` as the domain for labels and annotations - see https://k8s.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/
  - there are a couple of exceptions in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/audit-annotations/, FWIW
- if we document and register this `k8s.io/component` label, people may well confuse it with https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/#app-kubernetes-io-component and use the wrong thing

### What did you expect to happen?

I guess ideally we'd have proposed and then been able to review docs for this when it went alpha, and in that alternative history the discrepancy would have been much more obvious, and it could have been fixed earlier.

I think we should fix it so that we follow the convention of nearly every other annotation used in Kubernetes code.

Look at the source code. Any text editor would work.

windows cpu maximum incorrect with more than one processor group
### What happened?

When submitting a windows pod using resource limits on a node with more than one processor group, the specified `CpuMaximum` count is incorrect due to the usage of `runtime.NumCPU()` which does not take processor groups into account.

For example:
- node with 96 cores
- cpu limit 94
- `runtime.NumCPU()` returns `48`

This results in a CPU maximum of 10000 since the range is from [1, 10000]:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container_windows.go#L82..L91

```go
	limit := int64(94 * 1000)
	numCPU := 48
	fmt.Println(((10000 * limit) / int64(numCPU) / 1000))


```

Our initial goal for this was to limit a process to not use all available CPU and therefore render the node uncontrollable. 

### What did you expect to happen?

A CPU maximum of `9791` instead of `10000` for that specific case. For the calculation, it should use the CPU count for all available processor groups instead of just the current one. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Launch a node with a lot of CPUs, for example [a Azure Standard_D96a_v4](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/dav4-dasv4-series) and schedule the following pod on it:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: debug-windows
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - args:
    - ping /t 127.0.0.1
    command:
    - cmd
    - /c
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/windows/nanoserver:1809
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: main
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "94"
        memory: 300Gi
      requests:
        cpu: "90"
        memory: 200Gi
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/os: windows
```

Then SSH into the node and inspect the running container using `crictl.exe inspect <id>`. The `cpu_maximum` value will be set to 10000. 

### Anything else we need to know?

[tklauser/numcpus](https://github.com/tklauser/numcpus) (which just uses [`windows.GetActiveProcessorCount()`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sys/windows#GetActiveProcessorCount)) is able to correctly find out the number of CPUs available to a system. Using `golang.org/x/sys/windows` for calculation or incorporating that code might solve this issue.

Ephemeral container fails to be created for Static Pod
### What happened?

I created an ephemeral container for a Static Pod using the `kubectl debug` command. The command succeed.

```console
❯ kubectl debug --image=busybox --share-processes=true --target=kube-apiserver -n kube-system kube-apiserver-kind-control-plane -- sleep infinity
Targeting container "kube-apiserver". If you don't see processes from this container it may be because the container runtime doesn't support this feature.
Defaulting debug container name to debugger-vgkn4.
```



The API server accepted the ephemeral container:
```console
❯ kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-kind-control-plane --output=jsonpath='{.spec.ephemeralContainers}'
[{"command":["sleep","infinity"],"image":"busybox","imagePullPolicy":"Always","name":"debugger-vgkn4","resources":{},"targetContainerName":"kube-apiserver","terminationMessagePath":"/dev/termination-log","terminationMessagePolicy":"File"}]
```

However, the container is not created.

Its status is also not available:

```console
❯ kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-kind-control-plane --output=jsonpath='{.status.ephemeralContainerStatuses}'

```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these:

(a) the API server rejects the request to create an ephemeral container for a Static Pod
(b) kubelet creates the ephemeral container, and update the Static Pod's status sub-resource

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Using a recent version of [docker engine](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/), [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/)  v0.17 or newer, and [kubectl](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/#kubectl) v1.25.0 or newer, create a cluster and create an ephemeral container running `sleep infinity`. Since the ephemeral container is not running, the output of `grep` is 0. 

```
kind create cluster
kubectl debug --image=busybox --share-processes=true --target=kube-apiserver -n kube-system kube-apiserver-kind-control-plane -- sleep infinity
docker exec -it kind-control-plane ps -axw | grep --count "sleep infinity"
```


### Anything else we need to know?

The [Ephemeral Containers KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/277-ephemeral-containers/README.md) does not address Static Pods.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

Kubectl restmapping cache causes inconsistent behaviour in case of resource name conflict
### What happened?

I deployed a CRD (`teleportroles`) with the shortnames `role` and `roles`, conflicting with `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1`.

Initially `kubectl get role` and `kubectl get roles` were both returnning `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` resources.

I ran `kubectl get teleportrole`.

Now, `kubectl get role` return my CRs instead of `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` resources.

However `kubectl get roles` continues to return `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` resources.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect kubectl's behaviour to be consistent. The outcome of `kubectl get X` should not depend on the order the APIs were discovered and cached. I also expect exact names to be preferred over shortnames.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On a freshly kubectl context (not one you already used and might have cached RESTMappings):
- create a CRD with a shortname conflicting with another resource, `role` for example
- run `kubectl get role -n kube-sytem` (because there are roles by default there) and `kubectl get roles -n kube-system`
- observe the kube rbac resources are properly returned
- run `kubectl get yourcrd` once
- run `kubectl get role -n kube-sytem` (because there are roles by default there) and `kubectl get roles -n kube-system`
- observe the `kubectl get role` no longer returns the kubernetes roles, but `kubectl get roles` still does. 

### Anything else we need to know?

During initial resolution, [exact name matches are preferred](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/58861). It seems this property is not true anymore when doing cache lookups. When cache was populated by `kubectl get teleportroles`, it overrode the mapping `role` -> `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1`

I believe this is the same issue as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/59812

- For instance, we may want to rename `IsErrorRetryable` to `IsHttpErrRetryable` and `checkWait` to `isServerIndicatedRetry`. 
That would have helped bring this back into mental cache faster and possibly help some future refactorer.


### What did you expect to happen?

Maintain thread safety of `*Request`

If the underlying block device corresponding to the volume is accidentally disconnected from the node (due to network, hardware problem, etc...), the user cannot delete the pod. TITLE: revisit `PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` func from default preemption
SYMPTOM: #### What happened:
As the comment here explained, the logic of `PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` func from default preemption is not accurate enough, the deleting pod should be a preemption victim instead of normal deleted pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104030#discussion_r680138858

Quote from @Huang-Wei 

> PodEligibleToPreemptOthers currently checks if a nominated node has low-priority terminating pods, then it assumes those terminating pods are preempted by the preemptor. It's actually not that accurate - we should verify the terminating pods are exactly preemption victims; otherwise a possible case is: the victims have been physically deleted, and the terminating pods are due to regular deletion.



#### What you expected to happen:
Refine the logic to make sure the deleting pod is actually a preemption victim.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this i
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because the preemption logic assumed that any terminating pods on a node were victims of preemption, without verifying if those pods were actually marked as preemption victims. Consequently, normal pod deletions could incorrectly prevent preemption on nodes where it should be allowed. This happened due to lack of distinction between pods terminated by preemption and pods terminating for other reasons.
FIX: - A terminating pod on a node that is not caused by preemption won't prevent kube-scheduler from preempting pods on that node
- Rename 'PreemptionByKubeScheduler' to 'PreemptionByScheduler'

TITLE: Data race when creating isomorphic Events with an "k8s.io/client-go/tools/events".EventRecorder
SYMPTOM: **What happened**:

I wrote a test creating multiple isomorphic Events with an "k8s.io/client-go/tools/events".[EventRecorder](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/events/interfaces.go#L26) and stumbled upon a data race.

The data race happens in the [recordToSink](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L153) function. It seems that the Event Series field can be read and written at the same time by two different goroutines. [Read](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L178) [Write](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L168-L171).

This seems to happen in only one scenario:
- (1) a singleton Event is created
- (2) an isomorphic Event is created
- (1) lock addition to cache
- (2) wait for the lock to be released
- (1) unlock
- (2) lock + [create](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L168-L171) the Series
- (1) [read](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L209) the freshly created Series
- (1) singleton Event
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that the event cache locking is insufficiently scoped, allowing multiple goroutines to read and write the event series concurrently without proper synchronization. Specifically, the cache lock is released between initial update and final update with the server-returned event, causing data races and overwriting of cache entries. The code also reused pointers from the cache when recording events, leading to concurrent access conflicts on the same event object.
FIX: Fix a data race when emitting similar Events consecutively
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go, staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/events/eventseries_test.go

embed_text:
Sometime Liveness/Readiness Probes fail because of net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
**What happened**:
In my cluster sometimes readiness the probes are failing. But the application works fine.
```
Apr 06 18:15:14 kubenode** kubelet[34236]: I0406 18:15:14.056915   34236 prober.go:111] Readiness probe for "default-nginx-daemonset-4g6b5_default(a3734646-77fd-11ea-ad94-509a4c9f2810):nginx" failed (failure): Get http://172.18.123.127:80/: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

**What you expected to happen**:
Successful Readiness Probe.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
We have few clusters with different workloads.
Only in cluster with big number of short living pods we have this issue.
But not on all nodes.
We can't reproduce this error on other our clusters (that have same configuration but different workload).
How i found the issue?
I deployed a daemonset:
```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: default-nginx-daemonset
  namespace: default
  labels:
    k8s-app: default-nginx
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      name: default-nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: default-nginx
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - operator: Exists
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: "1"
            memory: "1Gi"
          requests:
            cpu: "1"
            memory: "1Gi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
```
Then i started to listen events on all pods of this daemonset.
After a couple of time i received next events:
```
Warning  Unhealthy  110s (x5 over 44m)  kubelet, kubenode20  Readiness probe failed: Get http://172.18.122.143:80/: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
Warning  Unhealthy  11m (x3 over 32m)  kubelet, kubenode10  Readiness probe failed: Get http://172.18.65.57:80/: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
....
```
Those events where on ~50% of pods of this daemonset.

On the nodes where the pods with failed probes was placed, I collected the logs of kubelet.
And there was errors like:
```
Apr 06 14:08:35 kubenode20 kubelet[10653]: I0406 14:08:35.464223   10653 prober.go:111] Readiness probe for "default-nginx-daemonset-nkwkf_default(90a3883b-77f3-11ea-ad94-509a4c9f2810):nginx" failed (failure): Get http://172.18.122.143:80/: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

I was thinking that sometimes the nginx in pod really response slowly.
For excluding this theory, I created a short script that curl the application in pod and store response time in a file:
```
while true; do curl http://172.18.122.143:80/ -s -o /dev/null -w  "%{time_starttransfer}\n" >> /tmp/measurment.txt; done;
```

I run this script on node where the pod is placed for 30 minutes and i get the following:
```
$ cat /tmp/measurment.txt | sort -u
0.000
0.001
0.002
0.003
0.004
0.005
0.006
0.007

$ cat /tmp/measurment.txt | wc -l
482670
```
There was `482670` measurements and the longest response time was `0.007`.

In logs of pod there are only message with response code 200 (from my requests and requests of readiness probes):
```
[06/Apr/2020:14:06:30 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "kube-probe/1.12" "-"
......
[06/Apr/2020:14:08:35 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "curl/7.47.0" "-"
[06/Apr/2020:14:08:35 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "curl/7.47.0" "-"
[06/Apr/2020:14:08:35 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "curl/7.47.0" "-"
......
[06/Apr/2020:14:08:41 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "kube-probe/1.12" "-"
```
It means that part of probes are successful.

Then i stopped the curl script (because the big number of logs).
I waited while new error with failed probe appears in kubelet logs.
```
Apr 06 18:15:14 kubenode13 kubelet[34236]: I0406 18:15:14.056915   34236 prober.go:111] Readiness probe for "default-nginx-daemonset-4g6b5_default(a3734646-77fd-11ea-ad94-509a4c9f2810):nginx" failed (failure): Get http://172.18.123.127:80/: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

And in logs of that pod with nginx I didn't find the request generated by this probe:

TITLE: Sometime Liveness/Readiness Probes fail because of net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
SYMPTOM: **What happened**:
In my cluster sometimes readiness the probes are failing. But the application works fine.
```
Apr 06 18:15:14 kubenode** kubelet[34236]: I0406 18:15:14.056915   34236 prober.go:111] Readiness probe for "default-nginx-daemonset-4g6b5_default(a3734646-77fd-11ea-ad94-509a4c9f2810):nginx" failed (failure): Get http://172.18.123.127:80/: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

**What you expected to happen**:
Successful Readiness Probe.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
We have few clusters with different workloads.
Only in cluster with big number of short living pods we have this issue.
But not on all nodes.
We can't reproduce this error on other our clusters (that have same configuration but different workload).
How i found the issue?
I deployed a daemonset:
```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: default-nginx-daemonset
  namespace: default
  labels:
    k8s-app: default-nginx
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      name: default-nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: default-nginx

ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that kubelet readiness and liveness probes open many short-lived network connections that enter the TIME-WAIT state, which by default lasts 60 seconds. This causes exhaustion of network resources like ephemeral ports and conntrack entries on nodes with many pods and high probe rates, leading to probe failures.
FIX: kubelet TCP and HTTP probes are more effective using networking resources: conntrack entries, sockets, ... 
This is achieved by reducing the TIME-WAIT state of the connection to 1 second, instead of the defaults 60 seconds. This allows kubelet to free the socket, and free conntrack entry and ephemeral port associated.
FILES: pkg/kubelet/prober/scale_test.go, pkg/probe/dialer_others.go, pkg/probe/dialer_windows.go, pkg/probe/http/http.go, pkg/probe/tcp/tcp.go

client-go: if an error occurs during request construction, URL() can return a useless result with no indication of an error
### What happened?

When constructing a `rest.Request`, _e.g._ to stream I/O from a pod:

```
	req := k8s.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().Resource("pods").Name(podName).Namespace(podNamespace).SubResource("exec")
	req.VersionedParams(&v1.PodExecOptions{
		Command: command,
		Stdin:   false,
		Stdout:  true,
		Stderr:  true,
		TTY:     true,
	}, scheme.ParameterCodec)
	exec, err := remotecommand.NewSPDYExecutor(config, "POST", req.URL())
```

if `req.err` ends up set, `req.URL()` will still return a result without indicating that something went wrong, resulting in a misleading error further down the line. (In my case, I wasn’t providing the correct scheme; the parameters therefore couldn’t be encoded, and the SPDY upgrade failed with an error saying that at least one of stdin, stdout or stderr had to be provided.)

### What did you expect to happen?

Other operations on `rest.Request` fails as appropriate if `req.err` is not `nil`; I would expect `URL()` to do so too. I realise that means a backwards-incompatible change.

Another solution could be to provide a `req.Error()` (same as on the response).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above, with any scheme other than client-go’s.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

CSI migration race condition can cause unexpected detach and data loss
### What happened?

After the cluster was updated to enable PD CSI Driver, there was a race condition where AD Controller (kube-controller-manager) started to [populate the desired state of world](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dc2898b20c6bd9602ae1c3b51333e2e4640ed249/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L438-L447) BEFORE the PD CSI Driver was up, thus AD Controller gave us the error 

```
Error creating spec for volume "elasticsearch", pod "XXX"/"elasticsearch-0": error performing CSI migration checks and translation for PVC "dXX"/"elasticsearch-elasticsearch-0": in-tree plugin kubernetes.io/gce-pd is migrated on node gke-stage-XXXXX but driver pd.csi.storage.gke.io is not installed.
```

Then AD Controller triggered the disk detach because the disk/volume was not populated in the desired state of world.

Unfortunately the disk was in use during this detach and got corrupted.

### What did you expect to happen?

Since cluster upgrades can cause the controller manager and CSI drivers to start at different times, the AD controller needs to be more conservative when detaching

TITLE: Watchcache doesn't distinguish the RV=0 and RV="" semantic for watches
SYMPTOM: As Jordan pointed out in:
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3667/files#r1055906242

watchcache treats RV=0 and RV="" the same way, even though it's not what we document:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/#semantics-for-watch

This should be fixed.
ROOT CAUSE: The watchcache incorrectly handled the resource version (RV) parameter by treating an unset RV ("" meaning no resource version specified) the same as RV=0, which violates the documented semantics. The implementation did not distinguish between these cases and therefore did not perform a quorum read or serve the watch from underlying storage when the RV was unset, causing inconsistent watch behavior.
FIX: cacher: If RV is unset, the watch is now served from the underlying storage as documented.
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher_whitebox_test.go

kube-apiserver doesn't reload the kubelet client certificate/key on each logs query
### What happened?

We bootstrap our clusters with kubeadm (through clusterapi), but provide our own end certs to shorten the certificate validity period.

Because of the shortened validity period, we rotate the file-based endcerts frequently. Recently we started noticing that after performing a certificate rotation, usage of `kubectl logs` was failing with

```sh
error: You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials)
```

From there, we looked at the kube-apiserver and kubelet logs and found log lines like the following:

```
"Unable to authenticate the request due to an error" err="verifying certificate SN=<REMOVED>, SKID=<REMOVED>, AKID=<REMOVED> failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2022-12-17T02:31:09Z is after 2022-12-17T00:16:30Z"
```

So it looks like kube-apiserver didn't reload the new kubelet client certificate. This issue typically goes away if we restart the kube-apiserver container or continue to run `kubectl logs` in a loop.

### What did you expect to happen?

Being able to replace/rotate the kube-apiserver kubelet client certificate/key without causing failure for any logs or node proxy commands/operations.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We were able to get a repro outside of our environment with the following steps.

1. Created a cluster-api cluster on azure with CAPZ using the standard quickstart flow plus some minor tweaks:
- Added ` kubelet-certificate-authority: /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt` as an apiserver argument.
- Added ` rotate-server-certificates: "true"` as a kubelet argument.
- Used kubernetes version 1.23.6 and 1.23.15
2. Manually approved the kubelet server certificate csrs using `kubectl certificate approve`
3. In one shell continually ran `kubectl logs` and `kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/<NODE_NAME>/proxy/logs`
4. ssh'd into the controlplane node in another shell. ran  `mv /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver-kubelet-client.crt /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver-kubelet-client.crt.bak` and vice-versa.

From these steps I was able to see `kubectl logs` commands be successful when there was no certificate file and failed when the certificate file was present. Eventually, the kube-apiserver picks up the up-to-date certificate/file.

I don't know the internals here, but it seems like kube-apiserver was using some sort of cached-connection which had the stale certificate.

### Anything else we need to know?

We believe this used to work in kubernetes v1.21 and below. Need to confirm this by spinning up downlevel clusters.

Kubernetes Jobs API rapid-fire scheduling doesnt honor exponential backoff characteristics
### What happened?

# Problem

The job controller appears to "rapidly reschedule" several pods at the same time (without backing off) which ultimately appears almost like a batch or gang scheduling workflow.  

... This is the opposite of what the job docs say, bc they clearly state :
```
 The back-off limit is set by default to 6. Failed Pods associated with the Job are recreated by the Job controller with an exponential back-off delay (10s, 20s, 40s ...) capped at six minutes.
```
So, rather then, 

- 10, 20, 40, 80 wait times between trying things we are seeing
- 0, 3, 3, 3, 3 second wait times before pods are being retried

This is in the 1.25 release, but not sure if it also happens earlier.  You can see this in the latest kind version. 



### What did you expect to happen?

Jobs wouldnt schedule the same pod at rapid fire intervals

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Thanks to Ryan for this reproducer: 
```

kind: Job

metadata:

  name: backoff-exp

spec:

'|sort

# Problem

The job controller appears to "rapidly reschedule" several pods at the same time (without backing off) which ultimately appears almost like a batch or gang scheduling workflow.  

... This is the opposite of what the job docs say, bc they clearly state :
```
 The back-off limit is set by default to 6. Failed Pods associated with the Job are recreated by the Job controller with an exponential back-off delay (10s, 20s, 40s ...) capped at six minutes.
```
So, rather then, 

- 10, 20, 40, 80 wait times between trying things we are seeing
- 0, 3, 3, 3, 3 second wait times before pods are being retried

This is in the 1.25 release, but not sure if it also happens earlier.  You can see this in the latest kind version. 



### What did you expect to happen?

Jobs wouldnt schedule the same pod at rapid fire intervals

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

# Details 

Thanks to Ryan for this reproducer: 
```
apiVersion: batch/v1

kind: Job

metadata:

  name: backoff-exp

spec:

  backoffLimit: 100

  template:

    spec:

      containers:

        - name: die

          image: ubuntu


ROOT CAUSE: The Job controller's back-off logic was coupled with the workqueue's back-off mechanism, causing rapid rescheduling of failed pods without proper exponential delay. This coupling meant multiple pod failures within a reconciliation cycle did not properly aggregate back-off delays, resulting in retries being scheduled too frequently and ignoring exponential backoff requirements.
FIX: The job controller back-off logic is now decoupled from workqueue. In case of parallelism > 1, if there are multiple new failures in a reconciliation cycle, all the failures are taken into account to compute the back-off. Previously, the back-off kicked in for all types of failures; with this change, only pod failures are taken into account. If the back-off limits exceeds, the job is marked as failed immediately; before this change, the job is marked as failed in the next back-off.

cacher watch timeout not handled when it is not ready
### What happened?

In one of our multi tenant cluster, we've observed that all kubelet requests (under `system-nodes` flow schema) eventually started timing out or aborted due to secret watch request occupying all `system` priority level concurrency share. It happened due to our KMS provider was quite latent (& sometimes failing) for brief amount of time. Due to high latency from KMS provider, all the cacher's reflector list & watch calls start failing (repeatedly retried) and cacher was marked as not ready.

Now all the watch request to the cacher was waiting for `ready` conditional variable and never timed out. This led all watch requests stuck in priority and fairness queue for ever & eventually occupying all the concurrency shares, affecting other requests belonging to same priority level.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f173d01c011c3574dea73a6fa3e20b0ab94531bb/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L457-L467

We need to handle watch timeout when cacher not ready to fix the issue.

### What did you expect to happen?

Watch requests to get time out eventually when cacher is not ready.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Consider a large cluster (5K nodes) having more than 50K number of secret resources encrypted using KMS provider and mounted by various pods in the cluster. Restart api server & artificially induce high latency on KMS provider (assuming we've configured lower dek cache size of 10 items) and wait for kubelet requests to start failing.

### Anything else we need to know?

May we can implement a way to timeout ready conditional variable (sync.Cond) `wait` function. Let me know if I can raise a pull request to fix this. Roughly along below lines:
```go
type ready struct {
	sync.RWMutex

	ok bool
	c chan struct{}
}

func newReady() *ready {
	return &ready{c: make(chan struct{}, 0)}
}

func (r *ready) wait() {
	r.waitChan(nil)
}

func (r *ready) waitChan(stop <-chan struct{}) {
	r.RLock()
	ok, c := r.ok, r.c
	r.RUnlock()
	if ok {
		return
	}
	select {
	case <-stop:
	case <-c:
	}
}


func (r *ready) check() bool {
	r.RLock()
	defer r.RUnlock()
	return r.ok
}

func (r *ready) set(ok bool) {
	r.Lock()
	r.ok = ok
	close(r.c) // broadcast
	r.c = make(chan struct{})
	r.Unlock()
}
```

Auto-closing issues is harmful and causes friction
Previously open issue : https://github.com/kubernetes/community/issues/5473
Twitter Discussion : https://twitter.com/BenTheElder/status/1407774856033181696

There's pros and cons to having a bot do this, let me try to enumerate current situation here:
- maintainers don't have to play bad cop
- keep set of open issues at a maintainable level
- bot commands are available to org members to `/reopen` reduces friction
- lifecycle labels help folks specify which issues not to touch
- we currently do not have dedicated team(s) that do issue triage well (except for some SIG like api-machinery that do this really well with twice a week triage session)
- initial issue labeling is still a problem, routing issues to the correct sig
- we have a new triage label which is not widely used yet across sigs

However there are numerous problems with the current situation:
- impression that project does not care about bugs
- folks open new issues for things that may be already present but closed
- too much traffic/noise from the bot activity
- issues where some follow up was requested/needed gets closed 

Options to do better?
- triage party 
- more hands on deck, train incoming folks to do issue triage and manage that as a subproject of some SIG
- stop the bot cold and let the SIGs adjust

What did i miss @BenTheElder ?



PS: It will be ironic if this issue gets auto-closed!

Mutation of a cached object in kubelet through in place resizing of pods
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76d351065e504e23b7962158ef0e9067b6bd96ed/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2682

mutates the pod object in place (vs creating a copy first).  That's illegal and can cause data races or potentially panics (the panic is unlikely here but I can't rule it out).

This line should be:

```
pod = updatedPod
...
kl.podManager.UpdatePod(pod)
```

This should be fixed because we might serialize the object in the middle of this from somewhere else and if the object changes midway the protobuf object we create may not be valid, leading to panics in kubelets with this gate turned on.



### What did you expect to happen?

No mutation of pod objects from within `Sync*Pod` methods (in fact no mutation of `pod` should occur in most loops).

API-initiated eviction does not work on first try in certain scenarios, but does work on second try 
### What happened?

Scenarios that require setting resourceVersion either

- explicitly to the eviction request
- or when the eviction API needs to make sure that the pod has not become ready when deleting unready pods https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction.go#L232

fails to evict a pod. This is caused by a conflict with PodDisruptionConditions feature, which adds a condition to a pod, and the delete itself fails. The second eviction works correctly and results in a pod deletion.

### What did you expect to happen?

eviction should succeed on a first try 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create a simple pod

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  containers:
    - name:  nginx
      image: registry.k8s.io/nginx-slim:0.8
```

```
$ kubectl apply -f nginx.yaml
```

2. obtain its resource version

```
$ kubectl get pod nginx -oyaml | grep resourceVersion
> resourceVersion: "313"
```

3. try to evict it

```
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF --raw /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx/eviction
{"apiVersion": "policy/v1", "kind": "Eviction", "metadata": {"name": "nginx"}, "deleteOptions": {"preconditions": {"resourceVersion": "313"}}}
EOF
$ Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on Pod "nginx": the ResourceVersion in the precondition (313) does not match the ResourceVersion in record (425). The object might have been modified
```

the eviction request fails, but we can see that the DisruptionTarget condition has been added to the pod

```
$ oc get pod nginx -oyaml | grep DisruptionTarget -B 5
>   - lastProbeTime: null
>    lastTransitionTime: "2023-03-13T21:29:04Z"
>    message: 'Eviction API: evicting'
>    reason: EvictionByEvictionAPI
>    status: "False"
>    type: DisruptionTarget
```

4. second eviction with updated resouce version succeeds


```
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF --raw /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx/eviction
{"apiVersion": "policy/v1", "kind": "Eviction", "metadata": {"name": "nginx"}, "deleteOptions": {"preconditions": {"resourceVersion": "520"}}}
EOF
> {"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{},"status":"Success","code":201}
```

ROOT CAUSE: The eviction API sets a precondition on the pod's ResourceVersion when deleting it to ensure consistency. embed_text:
Transition running deleted pods to a terminal phase
### What happened?

Running pods when deleted are not transitioned to a terminal phase, even when all containers are terminated. Note that, containers are not restarted for deleted pods: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/container/helpers.go#L73-L77.

This is problematic for jobs, which as a workaround categorizes all deleted pods (with `deletionTimestamp != nil`) as failed,
but it is still problematic:
- the replacement pod is created too early, leaving two running pods (for the same index) at the same time, which is a problem for some job frameworks. See related Issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115844.
- a pod categorized a failed by the job controller (due to the presence of deletionTimestamp) may end up succeeded if the pod's container completes successfully within the graceful termination period. 
- it blocks a related issue in Jobs: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113855.

The solution might be scoped to pods with finalizers to save a PATCH request to make the transitioning. 

Fixing this issue is planned as part of the Jobs KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3329

### What did you expect to happen?

Every deleted running pod is transitioned to a terminal phase if there is a finalizer.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod like this:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: running-pod
  finalizers: ["example.com/my-finalizer"]
spec:
  restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: centos:7
    command: ["bash"]
    args: ["-c", 'echo "Hello world" && sleep 1800']
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```
2. Delete the pod by `kubectl delete`
After 30s check the pod status with `kubectl get pods -oyaml`. You can see:

```yaml
    containerStatuses:
    - ...
      state:
        terminated:
          exitCode: 137
          reason: Error
    phase: Running
```
**Issue**: the pod remains the in the **Running** phase forever.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

TITLE: Transition running deleted pods to a terminal phase
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Running pods when deleted are not transitioned to a terminal phase, even when all containers are terminated. Note that, containers are not restarted for deleted pods: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/container/helpers.go#L73-L77.

This is problematic for jobs, which as a workaround categorizes all deleted pods (with `deletionTimestamp != nil`) as failed,
but it is still problematic:
- the replacement pod is created too early, leaving two running pods (for the same index) at the same time, which is a problem for some job frameworks. See related Issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115844.
- a pod categorized a failed by the job controller (due to the presence of deletionTimestamp) may end up succeeded if the pod's container completes successfully within the graceful termination period. 
- it blocks a related issue in Jobs: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113855.

The solution might be scoped to pods with finalizers to save a PATCH request to make the transitioning. 

Fixing this issue is planned as part of the Jobs KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3329

### What 
ROOT CAUSE: The kubelet did not transition deleted pods that are still in the Running or Pending phase to a terminal phase (Succeeded or Failed) even when their containers had terminated and would not be restarted due to their RestartPolicy. This caused deleted pods to remain stuck in Running or Pending state indefinitely.
FIX: Give terminal phase correctly to all pods that will not be restarted. 

In particular, assign Failed phase to pods which are deleted while pending. Also, assign a terminal 
phase (Succeeded or Failed, depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) to pods which
are deleted while running.

This fixes the issue for jobs using pod failure policy (with JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions 
feature gates enabled) that their pods could get stuck in the pending phase when deleted.

ACTION REQUIRED: Users who maintain controllers which relied on the fact that pods with RestartPolicy=Always
never enter the Succeeded phase may need to adapt their controllers. This is because as a consequence of 
the change pods which use RestartPolicy=Always may end up in the Succeeded phase in two scenarios: pod 
deletion and graceful node shutdown.
FILES: pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go, pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go, pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods_test.go, pkg/kubelet/kubelet_test.go, pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go, pkg/kubelet/pod_workers_test.go, pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go, pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager_test.go, pkg/kubelet/status/testing/fake_pod_deletion_safety.go, pkg/kubelet/status/testing/mock_pod_status_provider.go

kubectl apply requires CRDs to apply non-CRD resources if we use `kind: List`
### What happened?

kubectl apply performs validation before the apply. 

Non-CRD resources (e.g. pods / deployments) don't need CRD schema for validation, but if we use `kind: List` resource, kubectl calls `LIST apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions`.

TITLE: kubectl apply requires CRDs to apply non-CRD resources if we use `kind: List`
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

kubectl apply performs validation before the apply. 

Non-CRD resources (e.g. pods / deployments) don't need CRD schema for validation, but if we use `kind: List` resource, kubectl calls `LIST apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions`.
In my Kubernetes cluster, administrator doesn't allow users to list CRDs, so user cannot apply non-CRD resources (e.g. pods / deployments) with `kind: List` resource.


### What did you expect to happen?

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  labels:
    app: nginx
  name: nginx
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  strategy: {}
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged
        name: nginx-unprivileged
        resources: {}
status: {}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  labels:
    app: nginx2
  name: nginx2
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx2
  strategy: {}
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: n
ROOT CAUSE: The underlying cause is that the OpenAPI schema used during kubectl apply validation does not include an entry for the 'List' resource kind. As a result, the validation logic treats 'List' kinds as CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) and makes requests to the CRD API endpoint unnecessarily. This leads to issues when users lack permission to list CRDs, preventing them from applying non-CRD resources grouped in a 'List'.
FIX: Skip hasSupport check for List type

TITLE: Cacher may not send events if it reinitializes at the time of watch initialization
SYMPTOM: Found when reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116024

I'm still not 100% convinced it's true, but I believe this is a faulty scenario:
1. new watch is being established `Watch()` method
2. `c.ready` is still initialized so we successfully pass the c.ready.wait() check
3. `ListAndWatch` in `startCaching` fails (for whatever reason)
4. `c.ready.set(false)` is called (from defer in `startCaching`)
5. `startCaching` is called again and we call `terminateAllWatchers()`
6. the Watch call (started in point 1 above) only now continues to be processed and is established (and added to watchers) - init events are being send in the meantime
7. `ListAndWatch` is being called from `startCaching` which reinitializes watchCache to a new (higher RV)
8. if some events missed in the meantime, they will not be delivered to this newly established watch
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because the watch cache was being reinitialized concurrently with an incoming watch request. The watch request passed a readiness check based on stale state before the cache was reset, causing the watcher to be added after the cache was replaced at a higher resource version. As a result, events happened during the reinitialization window were missed by the new watcher, leading to lost events.
FIX: Fixed a rare race condition in kube-apiserver that could lead to missing events when a watch API request was created at the same time kube-apiserver was re-initializing its internal watch.
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher_whitebox_test.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/ready.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/ready_test.go

PVs with annotations are not being dynamically provisioned on k8s 1.26.1 
### What happened?

We observed that when deplying manifests to a cluster running 1.26.1-gke.200, the StorageClass and PVC get created successfully. However, the PVC is stuck in a Pending state and no PV is provisioned.

The workaround is to add storageClassName to one of the pending PVCs on cluster, and it did go from Pending to properly provisioned a PV and reaching Bound state. 

We looked at the logs and found that according to the doc: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#class,

```
In the past, the annotation volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class 
was used instead of the storageClassName attribute. This annotation
 is still working; however, it will become fully deprecated in a future 
Kubernetes release.
```

Is this annotation is fully deprecated in the new 1.26.1 release? If yes can we add this detail to documentation or release note?






### What did you expect to happen?

the PVC should not stuck in a Pending state and PV is provisioned in 1.26.1

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a 1.26.1-gke.200 cluster in GKE
2. Create via yaml

```

        env:
          - name: MY_POD_NAME
            valueFrom:
              fieldRef:
                fieldPath: metadata.name
        volumeMounts:

    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim

        requests:
          storage: 10Gi

The error comes form the code: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/915924e64d08b7b2d3e6da81840e46d96304cdc9/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller_base.go#L275 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/915924e64d08b7b2d3e6da81840e46d96304cdc9/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L2259

There are some hypotheses here:

The annotation volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class does not work on 1.26.1 any more, so a default storage class is being populated to the PVC.
For some reason, the [DefaultStorageClass admission controller](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#defaultstorageclass) did not work, so the PVC was deployed with an empty StorageClass nil.

TITLE: scheduler: data race between PodInfo.Update and PriorityQueue.AddNominatedPod
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

As part of adding support for dynamic resource allocation to `test/integration/scheduler_perf`, I ran `go test -race`. With DRA, scheduling failures occur, and that led to a race report:

```
$ go test -v -timeout=0 -bench=.*/SchedulingWithInlineResourceClaims/ -race ./test/integration/scheduler_perf

WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c000baafc0 by goroutine 25750:
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework.(*PodInfo).Update()
      /nvme/gopath/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go:216 +0xd2e
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue.updatePod()
      /nvme/gopath/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go:903 +0x5a4
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue.(*PriorityQueue).Update()
      /nvme/gopath/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go:620 +0x582
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler.(*Scheduler).updatePodInSchedulingQueue()
      /nvme/gopath/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go:140 +0x359
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler.(*Scheduler).updatePodInSchedulingQueue-fm()
      <autogenerated>:1 +0x6d
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.ResourceE
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because the PodNominator and the SchedulingQueue used separate locks to protect access to the same `*QueuedPodInfo` objects. When one goroutine updated a PodInfo while another simultaneously accessed it via a different lock, a data race happened. The issue was that the locking was not shared, which led to concurrent unsynchronized access.
FIX: Fixed data race in `kube-scheduler` when preemption races with a Pod update.
FILES: pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go, pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go, pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go, pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue_test.go, pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go

Cannot create ingress with ingressClass annotation and IngressClassName both set
### What happened?

An ingress resource with both `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set cannot be **created**. Ingress resources can be updated to include both the annotation and the `ingressClassName` without issue.

Kubernetes response:

> The Ingress "example-ingress" is invalid: annotations.kubernetes.io/ingress.class: Invalid value: "nginx": can not be set when the class field is also set


### What did you expect to happen?

The ingress should be deployed with both annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set, as it is supported by updating an existing ingress.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply this resource:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: example-ingress
  annotations:
    ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: test.foo.bar
    http:
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          backend:
            service:
              name: dummy-service
              port:
                number: 1234

```

The code causing this issue is here:

Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir
### What happened?

A status of Pod mounted NFS PV remain as terminating when a node shutdown and restart.

### What did you expect to happen?

A Pod is completely terminated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

### Summary

- Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV
- Shutdown the node where the Pod is running
- Wait for 5 min and the Pod status become `Terminating`
- Restart the node
- The Pod status is still `Terminating` and the Pod is never terminated completely

<details>

### Reproduce

Prepare a NFS Server.(I used `nfs-kernel-server`)  

Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV like this.  
`nfs-pv-test-pod.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    run: nfs-pv-test-pod
  name: nfs-pv-test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - image: ubuntu
    name: nfs-pv-test-pod
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while :; do sleep 10; done"]
    volumeMounts:
      - name: nfs-test-volume
        mountPath: "/srv"
  volumes:
    - name: nfs-test-volume
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: nfs-test-pvc
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: node02

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: nfs-test-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Mi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: nfs-test-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Mi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  nfs:
    server: <NFS Server IP Address>
    path: <NFS Server Dir Path>
```

Shutdown the node where the Pod is running.(In this case `node02`)
```console
root@node02:~# shutdown now
```

And the status of node02 becomes `NotReady`.
```console
$ k get no
NAME     STATUS     ROLES           AGE    VERSION
cp01     Ready      control-plane   126d   v1.25.0
node01   Ready      <none>          126d   v1.25.0
node02   NotReady   <none>          126d   v1.25.0
```

After 5 min later(by default), the Pod status becomes `Terminating`.  
(The time a Pod becomes `Terminating` status depends on `tolerationSeconds`.)  
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/#taint-based-evictions  
```console
$ k get po -owide -w 
NAME                    READY   STATUS        RESTARTS      AGE   IP            NODE     NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
nfs-pv-test-pod         1/1     Running       0             27m   10.0.160.99   node02   <none>           <none>

nfs-pv-test-pod         1/1     Running       0             28m   10.0.160.99   node02   <none>           <none>
nfs-pv-test-pod         1/1     Terminating   0             33m   10.0.160.99   node02   <none>           <none>
nfs-pv-test-pod         0/1     Terminating   0             38m   <none>        node02   <none>           <none>
nfs-pv-test-pod         0/1     Terminating   0             39m   <none>        node02   <none>           <none>
```

Then, restart the node and the status of node02 becomes `Ready`.
```console
$ k get no
NAME     STATUS     ROLES           AGE    VERSION
cp01     Ready      control-plane   126d   v1.25.0
node01   Ready      <none>          126d   v1.25.0
node02   Ready      <none>          126d   v1.25.0
```

But the Pod status is still `Terminating` and the Pod is never terminated completely.
```console
$ k get po 
NAME                    READY   STATUS        RESTARTS      AGE   IP            NODE     NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
nfs-pv-test-pod         0/1     Terminating   0             45m   <none>        node02   <none>           <none>
```

TITLE: Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

A status of Pod mounted NFS PV remain as terminating when a node shutdown and restart.

### What did you expect to happen?

A Pod is completely terminated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

### Summary

- Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV
- Shutdown the node where the Pod is running
- Wait for 5 min and the Pod status become `Terminating`
- Restart the node
- The Pod status is still `Terminating` and the Pod is never terminated completely

<details>

### Reproduce

Prepare a NFS Server.(I used `nfs-kernel-server`)  

Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV like this.  
`nfs-pv-test-pod.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    run: nfs-pv-test-pod
  name: nfs-pv-test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - image: ubuntu
    name: nfs-pv-test-pod
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while :; do sleep 10; done"]
    volumeMounts:
      - name: nfs-test-volume
        mountPath: "/srv"
  volumes:
    - name: nfs-test-volume
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: nfs-test-pvc
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: node02

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: n
ROOT CAUSE: The kubelet attempted to unmount a directory that was not actually mounted during pod termination, causing the unmount operation to fail and the pod to remain stuck in the Terminating state. This occurred because the code did not accurately check whether the target directory was indeed mounted before trying to unmount it.
FIX: Fix the problem Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir.

kube-scheduler: Bring back the ability to stop at the first failed filter
#108829 changed the default behavior of scheduler framework's `RunFilterPlugins` - from stopping at the first failed filter to always running all filters. This change breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale. Cluster Autoscaler imports the scheduler framework to simulate filters on artificial nodes. In a (pretty common) one-pod-per-node scenario, the number of `RunFilterPlugins` calls is ~quadratic wrt. the number of nodes needed for unschedulable pods - it can be a lot of calls. Before #108829, in such scenario the vast majority of `RunFilterPlugins` calls would stop at failing Fit or NodeAffinity filters, and not run the rest of them (e.g. PV-related filters). After the change, every call to `RunFilterPlugins` runs all filters, which completely breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale (an example scenario of 300 1-pod-per-node pods and 200 node groups takes >10min in 1.24, and ~50s in <1.22).

Can we get the old behavior back? Or re-introduce the config option so that Cluster Autoscaler can set it accordingly? Ideally, we'd also like to get this backported as far as possible (the change was introduced in 1.24).

Discovery memCacheClient has inconsistent error behavior with other DiscoveryInterfaces
### What happened?

I think this got stale and closed because it was posted on `kubernetes/client-go` but is still very relevant:
https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/issues/745

The [memCacheClient](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/f81a9405fae9d2a97f479bab1ab540fad1d2f178/discovery/cached/memory/memcache.go#L47) created by memory.NewMemCacheClient(...) returns an error when calling ServerResourcesForGroupVersion if the APIResources list returned is empty, as seen here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/6d14209323d355841b67c4d9ca8c22fb1ca930a6/discovery/cached/memory/memcache.go#L214-L216

Our particular case came up due to the `external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` API group being registered with the API server, but having no resources.

### What did you expect to happen?

If using [NewMemcachedDiscoveryClient](https://github.com/kubecfg/kubecfg/blob/4b23b794b8281c7886b5fd0bd03d7a38db876c10/cmd/root.go#L425) like [here](https://github.com/kubecfg/kubecfg/blob/4b23b794b8281c7886b5fd0bd03d7a38db876c10/pkg/kubecfg/validate.go#L48) to discover `apiservices` with zero current resources there should not be an error returned.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Do a discovery with a [memCacheClient](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/f81a9405fae9d2a97f479bab1ab540fad1d2f178/discovery/cached/memory/memcache.go#L47) against a Kubernetes cluster that has at least one `apiservice` with zero resources. The condition on the server that triggers the described issue can be expressed as e.g.:
```
$ kubectl get --raw /apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1
{"kind": "APIResourceList","apiVersion":"v1","groupVersion":"external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1","resources":[]}
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I would be good to get to know the reasoning behind the emptiness check in the `memCacheClient`, maybe there is good reason for it.

### Kubernetes version

<details>
Client Version: v1.20.15
Server Version: v1.22.8-gke.202
</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
Google Cloud (GKE)
</details>

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

We have a test that creates a static pod on every node and a daemonset that later deletes the manifests for those files.  Sometimes the mirror pod and the containerd pod remain.  We've seen this when transient failures communicating with the apiserver caused a failure in calico like:
```

ROOT CAUSE: The kubelet's housekeeping loop stopped processing updates for pods that were force deleted and no longer present in the config, which caused the pod worker to never receive the triggers needed to advance the pod's state machine during termination errors from the container runtime. TITLE: Improve readiness times for clusters that use envelope encryption and create large numbers of secrets.
SYMPTOM: **What would you like to be added**:
Remove the need to call remote KMS for every new Secret.

**Why is this needed**:
Due to the serial processing of List requests, the initialization of informers may take significant time due to the large number of consecutive trips to KMS. For example, assuming a 40 milliseconds round-trip to a KMS and two thousand secrets, the initialization of an informer may take 80 seconds.

Relevant PRs:
Reduce the number of trips to KMS by caching DEKs. #87438
Transform from storage concurrently during List operation. #88633
ROOT CAUSE: The bug was caused by the KMSv2 encryption implementation creating a new data encryption key (DEK) for every Secret encryption operation, which required remote calls to the KMS service. This design caused a large number of sequential KMS round-trips, leading to slow informer readiness times especially with large numbers of secrets.
FIX: The API server now re-uses data encryption keys while the kms v2 plugin's key ID is stable.  Data encryption keys are still randomly generated on server start but an atomic counter is used to prevent nonce collisions.

client-go/kubectl rejects discovery API responses with charset encoding info
We are using `client-go` (and `kubectl`) to interact with Kubernetes clusters behind a couple of proxy layers. One of these proxies completes the `Content-Type` headers to include character encoding details.

This was working fine until recently, when client-go/kubectl have started to fail when interacting with the discovery API. It seems that a recent change has made kubectl more restrictive of the content-type that it expects. I suspect that it is related to this commit: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/commit/25d5761bfa0603c77cf5efefb14fd2e63a03a773

For example, this is an error from a kubectl command:
```
...
E0422 16:28:02.626222   86629 memcache.go:265] couldn't get current server API group list: Unknown discovery response content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
I0422 16:28:02.626258   86629 cached_discovery.go:120] skipped caching discovery info due to Unknown discovery response content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
I0422 16:28:02.626346   86629 shortcut.go:100] Error loading discovery information: Unknown discovery response content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...
```

We can of course try to fix it on our end, removing that charset information. However, it is a valid content-type and the way kubectl is handling the content-type there seems like it is relying on implementation details of kube-apiserver (that it does not add metadata to the content-type). I propose to fix this issue in `kubectl`, by properly parsing and handling the content-type.

Strategic Merge does not handle directives for empty slices. 
### What happened?

When performing a strategic merge for a slice of maps with `patchStrategy=merge`, directives in the patch slice are ignored if the original list is empty. Instead, the merged slice still contains the directives. This causes the patched object to fail subsequent validation since it has directives in a slice.

This behavior can be seen if one attempts to patch `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.admissionregistration.k8s.io` specifically changes to the optional field [Webhooks](https://github.com/kubernetes/api/blob/master/admissionregistration/v1beta1/types.go#L93-L97).

If the original object has the following value
``` json
{
    "apiVersion": "admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1",
    "kind": "ValidatingWebhookConfiguration",
    "metadata": {
        "creationTimestamp": "2023-04-19T13:41:39Z",
        "generation": 2,
        "name": "base-validation",
        "resourceVersion": "200160",
        "uid": "70d47b26-ddba-430a-82d2-3fe7f8b4b840"
    }
}
```
And we attempt to do a strategic patch with the following information 
``` json
{
    "$setElementOrder/webhooks": [
        {
            "name": "new.foo.com"
        }
    ],
    "webhooks": [
        {
            "admissionReviewVersions": [
                "v1"
            ],
            "clientConfig": {
                "url": "https://foo.com"
            },
            "name": "new.foo.com",
            "sideEffects": "None"
        },
        {
            "$patch": "delete",
            "name": "foo.bar.com"
        }
    ]
}
```
The resulting object will look like the following JSON and fail validation.
``` json
{
    "apiVersion": "admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1",
    "kind": "ValidatingWebhookConfiguration",
    "metadata": {
        "creationTimestamp": "2023-04-19T13:41:39Z",
        "generation": 2,
        "name": "base-validation",
        "resourceVersion": "200160",
        "uid": "70d47b26-ddba-430a-82d2-3fe7f8b4b840"
    },
    "webhooks": [
        {
            "admissionReviewVersions": [
                "v1"
            ],
            "clientConfig": {
                "url": "https://foo.com"
            },
            "name": "new.foo.com",
            "sideEffects": "None"
        },
        {
            "$patch": "delete",
            "name": "foo.bar.com"
        }
    ]
}
```
Errors:
```
The ValidatingWebhookConfiguration "base-validation" is invalid: 
* webhooks[1].sideEffects: Required value: must specify one of None, NoneOnDryRun
* webhooks[1].clientConfig: Required value: exactly one of url or service is required
* webhooks[1].admissionReviewVersions: Required value: must specify one of v1, v1beta1
```


### What did you expect to happen?

Strategic merge always handles any directives in the patch.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

## Repo steps with kubectl
1. Apply the following webhook configuration `kubectl apply`
    ``` yaml
    apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
    kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
    metadata:
      name: base-validation
    webhooks:
      - name: foo.bar.com
        admissionReviewVersions:
          - "v1"
        clientConfig:
          url: https://foo.com
        sideEffects: None
    ```
2. Edit the newly created webhook and remove the Webhooks list. `kubectl edit validatingwebhookconfiguration base-validation`

3. Attempt to apply the following webhook configuration with `kubectl apply`
      ``` yaml
      apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
      kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
      metadata:
        name: base-validation
      webhooks:
        - name: new.foo.com
          admissionReviewVersions:
            - "v1"
          clientConfig:
            url: https://foo.com
          sideEffects: None
    ```

Notice that the request fails with the following errors
```
The ValidatingWebhookConfiguration "base-validation" is invalid: 
* webhooks[1].sideEffects: Required value: must specify one of None, NoneOnDryRun
* webhooks[1].clientConfig: Required value: exactly one of url or service is required
* webhooks[1].admissionReviewVersions: Required value: must specify one of v1, v1beta1
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The logic causing this behavior for the example can be seen here in [apimachinery](https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/master/pkg/util/strategicpatch/patch.go#L1179-L1194)
In this code, we see that if the original value was not found, we blindly assign the `patchFieldValue`

`volume.SetVolumeOwnership()` always fails when called for wrapped volume
### What happened?

Every time `volume.SetVolumeOwnership(ed)` from `empty_dir.go` is called for a projected volume, it fails with "no such file or directory" error.

The problem comes from the fact that `SetVolumeOwnership()` always calculates the root dir for ownership changes as `mounter.GetPath()` while projected.go explicitly passes another dir as the first arg of `SetUpAt()` call:
```
	if err := wrapped.SetUpAt(dir, mounterArgs); err != nil {
		return err
	}
```
(see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/96306f144a3c917a97fe27c9ad5dd89e4213f741/pkg/volume/projected/projected.go#L203)

### What did you expect to happen?

`volume.SetVolumeOwnership()` must succeed when a projected volume is created.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Print return value of `volume.SetVolumeOwnership()` when called from `empty_dir.go`:

@@ -280,7 +280,10 @@ func (ed *emptyDir) SetUpAt(dir string, mounterArgs volume.MounterArgs) error {
                err = fmt.Errorf("unknown storage medium %q", ed.medium)

TITLE: daemonset stuck in `Completed` state after a reboot (with graceful kubelet shutdown)
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

I can reproduce this reliably with Calico v3.25.0 CNI, installed straight from the upstream [manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/projectcalico/calico/v3.25.0/manifests/calico.yaml).

It seems to be a **regression** in Kubernetes 1.27.0-rc.0 compared to 1.27.0-beta.0, at least I can't reproduce it with beta.0.

Cluster is deployed, and everything is ready & healthy. After a series of node reboots some `calico-node` pods are stuck in `Completed` state and never recover:

```
NAMESPACE       NAME                                                   READY   STATUS      RESTARTS        AGE     IP               NODE                           NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
kube-system     calico-kube-controllers-6c99c8747f-q5g8d               1/1     Running     2 (14m ago)     26m     192.168.62.135   talos-default-controlplane-2   <none>           <none>

kube-system     calico-node-hvws2                                      1/1     Running     2 (11m ago)     25m  
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because in Kubernetes 1.27, the DaemonSet controller stopped recreating pods in the Succeeded (Completed) phase. Memory leak in kubelet volume_manager populator processedPods
### What happened?

If a pod is created and then deleted an entry in processedPods map remains forever (sometimes, it's racy).

The problem comes from the fact that `podWorker` calls volume_manager `WaitForUnmount()` asynchronously. If the last call happens after populator cleaned up resources, an entry is added to processedPods and will never be seen.

### What did you expect to happen?

An entry in processedPods map must be deleted if pod doesn't exist and pod runtime should removed according to `dswp.podStateProvider`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To verify that the issue really exists I applaied a simple [patch](https://github.com/jsafrane/kubernetes/commit/40ffc8e62836244ea6cffde8b9dff2c402d058c5) printing resources in `processedPods` map. Here is a reproducer:

1. Start brand-new fresh k8s cluster with `hack/local-up-cluster.sh`
2. Check entries in `processedPods`:
```
I0321 15:03:42.131049    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:03:43.131815    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 1
```
3. Create a pod, check its uid:
```
$ k get po fdroot -o yaml |grep uid
  uid: a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a
```
4. Verify that this uid is accurately reported:
```
I0321 15:05:06.193326    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 2
I0321 15:05:06.193412    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:05:06.193434    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a: true
```
5. Delete the pod, wait for a few mins, check for `processedPods` again:
```
I0321 15:48:29.113233    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 3
I0321 15:48:29.113252    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:48:29.113259    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a: false
I0321 15:48:29.113262    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod 213bcdcb-c9e7-4d96-af41-353d651cbd86: true
```

The entry `a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a: false` will be kept forever because kubelet doesn't know anything about this pod anymore:
```
$ k get pods --all-namespaces -o yaml |grep "a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a"
$
```
so no more events will ever come to populater for this uid, and the loop in `findAndRemoveDeletedPods()` won't find it because it was already deleted from `dswp.desiredStateOfWorld`.

### Anything else we need to know?

n/a

Currently, when loadbalancer service's ipFammilies updated，service controller will ignore this event. That means cloud provider can't update ipv4/ipv6 backend.
