code at :https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider/blob/fa271f103b481b342ed5eefd9cde68c30bf3b114/controllers/service/controller.go#L526

### Why is this needed?

Our load balancer supports dual-stack. When the services in the cluster are updated from IPv4 to IPv6(same ipv6->ipv4、ipv4->ipv4/ipv6), it is expected that the cloud provider can perceive this event and update the IPv4/IPv6 address to the backend of the load balancer.
ROOT CAUSE: The service controller was not observing updates to the ipFamilies field of load balancer services. As a result, changes in IP family configuration (e.g., switching between single-stack and dual-stack) did not trigger update events, preventing the cloud provider from adjusting the backend accordingly.
FIX: service controller trigger update when service ipfamilies changes
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go, staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller_test.go

embed_text:
Last apiserver to shutdown doesn't remove its IP from k8s svc endpoints
### What happened?

As part of the apiserver's pre-shutdown sequence, we stop the lease-controller from renewing the apiserver's etcd lease anymore and delete the lease:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/125e38c0872521bec49351415cc9fb624b046659/pkg/controlplane/controller.go#L211-L215

As part of the `RemoveEndpoints` call we expect that after the lease is deleted, the apiserver's IP is also removed from the k8s service endpoints object:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/125e38c0872521bec49351415cc9fb624b046659/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L315-L321

However, `doReconcile` isn't removing the IP if it's the last remaining one:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/125e38c0872521bec49351415cc9fb624b046659/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L210-L215

The comment there is assuming that `doReconcile` is always called after renewing the lease, which is incorrect since it can also be called as part of the shutdown workflow.

### What did you expect to happen?

The IP of the apiserver (even though it's the last one remaining) should be removed from k8s svc endpoints on shutdown.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Shutdown the last apiserver of the cluster and you'll see logs like this:

```
I1031 17:34:49.517758      12 controller.go:181] Shutting down kubernetes service endpoint reconciler
E1031 17:34:49.534880      12 controller.go:184] no master IPs were listed in storage, refusing to erase all endpoints for the kubernetes service
```

And the audit logs also confirm that the IP isn't removed from k8s endpoints object.

### Anything else we need to know?

Why is the above an issue?

If the IP isn't removed from the k8s endpoints object, clients (using in-cluster API mode) will try to continue talking/connecting to that instance even after the apiserver is dead. There are at least two issues with this:
- Causes confusing `i/o timeout` and `connection refused` errors for clients, instead of a cleaner `no route to host` error
- If the apiserver pod is restarted by kubelet (let's say due to healthcheck failure), clients may start talking to it prematurely even without healthz/readyz passing. This is not a recommended behavior ([xref](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/health-checks/)) as a bunch post-startup hooks like informer sync, internal controllers, etc may not have initialized yet

TITLE: NodePort will not listen on external IP if same IP is used as loadBalancerIP
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Hey, after upgrading kubernetes from 1.22 to 1.23, I'm experiencing strange service provisioning behavior using nodePort. I'm using kube-proxy (ipvs) + calico + metallb. 
If external IP is used by another service type (Loadbalancer - allocated by metallb), then the node owning this IP doesn't listen to NodePort on this interface.  
Unfortunately, I can't find any changes that could be causing this, any ideas?
Kubernetes 1.23
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  annotations:
    metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs: externalip1
  name: service
spec:
  ports:
  - name: client
    port: 31010
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: client
  type: LoadBalancer
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: service2
spec:
  ports:
  - appProtocol: http
    name: http
    nodePort: 32080
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: http
  - appProtocol: https
    name: https
    nodePort: 32443
    port: 443
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: https
  type: NodePort
```
``` console
ipvsadm -Ln | grep externalip1
node1:
    TCP  externalip1:31010 lc
    TCP  externalip1:32010 lc
node2:
    TCP  externalip1:31010 lc
ROOT CAUSE: In IPVS proxy mode, node IP addresses that were set as LoadBalancer IPs were also assigned to the kube-ipvs0 interface. Since NodePort services listen on all addresses except those assigned to kube-ipvs0, the NodePort ports on those node IPs that were also used as LoadBalancer IPs were excluded, causing the NodePort not to listen on those interfaces.
FIX: Fixes a 1.26 regression in kube-proxy ipvs mode
FILES: pkg/proxy/ipvs/netlink.go, pkg/proxy/ipvs/netlink_linux.go, pkg/proxy/ipvs/netlink_unsupported.go, pkg/proxy/ipvs/proxier.go, pkg/proxy/ipvs/testing/fake.go, pkg/proxy/ipvs/testing/fake_test.go

I1125 10:20:43.948819 3908451 reconciler.go:396] "operationExecutor.UnmountDevice started f

CSI volumes left overs are not cleaned up if CSI plugin is attachable
### What happened?

1. Create a Deployment or SS that uses a vsphere CSI volumes (for example).
2. Shutdown the node while pod was running.
3. Wait for node to go `NotReady` and pod to switch to `Terminating` state. 
4. Bring back the node up.
5. If the pod migrates to different node (or pod gets deleted), then files/directories inside `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/xxxx` should be cleaned up.

1. The volume types that are attachable, kubelet expects `node-publish-path` to be a mount point during reconstruction. So if node is rebooted then reconstruction fails because `/mount` path is not a mount point.
2. Kubelet tries to "Cleanup" the volume, but CSI driver may be unavailable at this point.
3. As a result volumes are never cleaned up.

Filesystem resize is required after snapshot restore / volume clone
Kubernetes should resize filesystem on a volume when it's created as a clone of a smaller volume / smaller snapshot is restored into it.

Example:
1. User takes a snapshot of 1 GiB volume with ext3 filesystem on it.
2. User restores the snapshot into 2 GiB volume.
    2.1 CSI driver restores the snapshot into a bigger volume, but ext3 filesystem still uses only 1 GiB of space.
3. CSI driver should make sure that the filesystem on the volume has been resized before the volume is mounted into a pod.

There are few steps needed:

* [x] Clarify behavior of `CreateVolume` CSI call, https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/pull/452
* [ ] Update CSI drivers to the new behavior.
  * [x] Move filesystem resize code from kubernetes/kuberenetes to kubernetes/mount-utils, so all CSI drivers can re-use the same code https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99039 
  * [x] Enhance the code above to compare the volume size from block device perspective and from filesystem perspective. See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-ebs-csi-driver/pull/595 for proof of concept. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99042
  * [ ] File issues in all community CSI drivers that we care about & fix them.
* [ ] Update csi-tests to (optionally?) check for volume size when cloning / restoring snapshot to a bigger size. https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-test/issues/325

APIServices can be deleted at the apiserver startup
### What happened?

Initially reported at 1.24.10, but it seems to be present in master as well:

We observe that a part of apiservices objects have been removed by "system:apiserver" right after the kubernetes upgrade.

It looks like there is race between "autoregister controller" [1] deleting apiservices and "crd-autoregister controller" populating a map of desired apiservices, i.e. in logs we see:
```
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070841Z Starting autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070858Z Waiting for caches to sync for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071116Z Starting crd-autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071128Z Waiting for caches to sync for crd-autoregister
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.270943Z Caches are synced for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.471323Z Caches are synced for crd-autoregister
```

The unwanted APIServices delete happened at 14:21:35.438 GMT so between crd-autoregister sync and autoregister controller.

It looks like we attempt to wait with "autoregister controller" for crd-autoregister to initialize here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c1d2d4295f9b4eb12bfbf6429fdf989f2ca8a02/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go#L148-L154

but for some reason we don't enter the if branch.

@liggitt tried adding this diff at HEAD:
```
diff --git a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go b/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
index 397c151e66a..8b755ab3179 100644
--- a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
+++ b/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
@@ -148,7 +148,11 @@ func createAggregatorServer(aggregatorConfig *aggregatorapiserver.Config, delega
 			// this prevents the autoregistration controller's initial sync from deleting APIServices for CRDs that still exist.
 			// we only need to do this if CRDs are enabled on this server.  We can't use discovery because we are the source for discovery.
 			if aggregatorConfig.GenericConfig.MergedResourceConfig.ResourceEnabled(apiextensionsv1.SchemeGroupVersion.WithResource("customresourcedefinitions")) {
+				klog.Infof("waiting for initial CRD sync...")
 				crdRegistrationController.WaitForInitialSync()
+				klog.Infof("initial CRD sync complete...")
+			} else {
+				klog.Infof("CRD API not enabled, starting APIService registration without waiting for initial CRD sync")
 			}
 			autoRegistrationController.Run(5, context.StopCh)
 		}()
```
and then started a default cluster with local-up-cluster gave:
```
I0518 08:31:16.826743   94479 aggregator.go:155] CRD API not enabled, starting APIService registration without waiting for initial CRD sync
```

which suggest we have a bug in master and the bug is around the "customresourcedefinitions if"

### What did you expect to happen?

APIServices are not deleted, there is no race between crd-autoregister and autoregister controllers

Restart apiserver with apiservices from crds?

Add a patch proposed by liggit@ and watch the initialization race.

Initially reported at 1.24.10, but it seems to be present in master as well:

We observe that a part of apiservices objects have been removed by "system:apiserver" right after the kubernetes upgrade.

It looks like there is race between "autoregister controller" [1] deleting apiservices and "crd-autoregister controller" populating a map of desired apiservices, i.e. in logs we see:
```
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070841Z Starting autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070858Z Waiting for caches to sync for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071116Z Starting crd-autoregister controller

`ResourceQuota` with "PriortyClass" as its scope is not calculated properly
### What happened?

If a Pod is subjected to a `ResourceQuota` with "PriortyClass" as its scope, the quota's calculation is incorrect. See repo steps for more details.

### What did you expect to happen?

`ResourceQuota` with "PriortyClass" as its scope can be calculated at all times.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a PriorityClass named "p1"

apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: p1
value: 100
```

  name: quota-p4

  hard:

    limits.cpu: "4"
    limits.memory: 2000Gi
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: 400Gi
  scopes:
  - PriorityClass <=== Notice this line

kube-proxy: traffic to healthcheck host ports is dropped because of iptables rule order
### What happened?

We are running self managed Kubernetes clusters on GCP and use Services of `type: LoadBalancer` with both public and private `EXTERNAL-IP`s to create load balancers for our clusters. Since upgrading kube-proxy to 1.26.3 (from 1.25.5) we saw that all healthchecks from GCP started to fail and traffic is now blindly load balanced across all nodes, which broke Services with
`externalTrafficPolicy` set to `Local`.
The issue seems to be introduced with this change: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108460
Here, `KUBE-IPVS-IPS` ipset is introduced and is used in iptables on chain `KUBE-IPVS-FILTER` as:
```
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-LOAD-BALANCER dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-CLUSTER-IP dst,dst -j RETURN                                                                                                                                           
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m set --match-set KUBE-IPVS-IPS dst -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable 
```
`KUBE-IPVS-IPS` seems to include external IPs (as also noted here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117613 and here: https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/issues/7183#issuecomment-1491205024) so the last rule above is dropping packets to external IPs that are not routed before reaching this point.
The next chain in iptables is `KUBE-NODE-PORT` and contains a single rule:
```
-A KUBE-NODE-PORT -m comment --comment "Kubernetes health check node port" -m set --match-set KUBE-HEALTH-CHECK-NODE-PORT dst -j ACCEPT
```
which seems specific to route packets arriving to health check ports

Workarounds to get health checks to work again from GCP are to either flush `KUBE-IPVS-IPS` ipset (temporary since kube-proxy will fight back) or move the ule to route packets to health check packets on top of `KUBE-IPVS-FILTER`:
```
sudo iptables -I KUBE-IPVS-FILTER 1 -m comment --comment "Kubernetes health check node port" -m set --match-set KUBE-HEALTH-CHECK-NODE-PORT dst -j ACCEPT
```


### What did you expect to happen?

Health checks from GCP should continue to work as intended after upgrading kube-proxy from 1.25.5 to 1.26.3

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use kube-proxy v1.26.3 in a Kubernetes cluster on GCP and create a Service of type `LoadBalancer`. Health checks from GCP should fail on all nodes

### Anything else we need to know?

Rolling back to v1.25.5 seems to fix the issue, even though we have to roll to fresh nodes to clean up everything and make health checks work again.

### Kubernetes version

TITLE:  kube-proxy: traffic to healthcheck host ports is dropped because of iptables rule order
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

We are running self managed Kubernetes clusters on GCP and use Services of `type: LoadBalancer` with both public and private `EXTERNAL-IP`s to create load balancers for our clusters. Since upgrading kube-proxy to 1.26.3 (from 1.25.5) we saw that all healthchecks from GCP started to fail and traffic is now blindly load balanced across all nodes, which broke Services with
`externalTrafficPolicy` set to `Local`.
The issue seems to be introduced with this change: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108460
Here, `KUBE-IPVS-IPS` ipset is introduced and is used in iptables on chain `KUBE-IPVS-FILTER` as:
```
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-LOAD-BALANCER dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-CLUSTER-IP dst,dst -j RETURN                                                                                                                                           
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m set --match-set KUBE-IPVS-IPS dst -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable 
```
`KUBE-IPVS-IPS` seems to include external IPs (as al
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause of the bug is that the iptables rule ordering in the KUBE-IPVS-FILTER chain wrongly rejected packets to healthCheckNodePorts on loadBalancer IPs, due to a restrictive rule introduced to reject new connections to IPVS IPs except for known service IPs. This rule blocked healthcheck traffic from GCP to the node ports for health checking, causing probes to fail. The healthCheckNodePort accept rule was missing in the iptables filter chain prior to the rejecting rule, causing legitimate healthcheck traffic to be dropped.
FIX: fixes 1.26 regression in kube-proxy ipvs accepting healthCheckNodePorts on the loadBalancerIP
FILES: pkg/proxy/ipvs/proxier.go

PV recycler fails if too many files in top-level directory
### What happened?

PV recycler pod fails to remove files if there are `>67567` files in the directory. 

Error in the pod logs:
```
› kl recycler-for-pv-040
2023-04-10T08:17:49.426784970Z /bin/sh: 1: rm: Argument list too long
```

Apparently one hits ARG_MAX due to too long command line. 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11289551/argument-list-too-long-error-for-rm-cp-mv-commands



### What did you expect to happen?

PV is recycled successfully

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Claim and NFS pv, create `>67567` files.

```
for i in {001..67568}
do
    echo hello > "/tmp/test/file${i}.txt"
done

# rm /tmp/test/*
-bash: /usr/bin/rm: Argument list too long
```




### Anything else we need to know?

In my testing I have provided my template and replaced the [current command](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/plugins.go#L1068) 

```
test -e /scrub && rm -rf /scrub/..?* /scrub/.[!.]* /scrub/*  && test -z "$(ls -A /scrub)" || exit 1
```

with:
```
test -e /scrub && find /scrub -mindepth 1 -delete && test -z "$(ls -A /scrub)" || exit 1
```

and recycle was successful. 


Maybe I am missing something but the `find -delete` was able to clean up everything (files, folders) and we also need to exclude the `/scrub` folder name.

`debian-base:v2.0.0` already has the `find` command, no changes to image needed.

In-tree vSphere volumes are not detached after KCM restart
### What happened?

I am enabling CSI migration on a vSphere cluster. A node was fully drained, all its Pods are deleted, but just before KCM detaches in-tree vSphere volume volumes from it, KCM restarts. A new KCM starts, sees attached volumes in `node.status.volumesAttached` that are not needed by any Pod on the node and calls vSphere in-tree volume plugin `Detach()`.

The in-tree vSphere volume plugin + cloud provider marks the volume as detached right away, without reaching to vCenter API. The volume remains attached forever.

I don't think it's related to CSI migration, IMO a regular node drain + KCM restart at the same time can cause the same issue.

KCM logs:

```
I0404 14:58:42.423920       1 operation_generator.go:1637] Verified volume is safe to detach for volume "nil" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") on node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" 
I0404 14:58:42.423986       1 nodemanager.go:359] No VM found for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk". Initiating rediscovery.
E0404 14:58:42.434007       1 nodemanager.go:362] Error "No VM found" node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
I0404 14:58:42.434051       1 nodemanager.go:395] node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
E0404 14:58:42.434074       1 vsphere.go:651] Cannot find node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" in cache. Node not found!!!
E0404 14:58:42.434101       1 attacher.go:287] Error checking if volume ("[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") is already attached to current node ("jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk"). Will continue and try detach anyway. err=No VM found
I0404 14:58:42.434114       1 nodemanager.go:359] No VM found for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk". Initiating rediscovery.
E0404 14:58:42.434127       1 nodemanager.go:362] Error "No VM found" node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
I0404 14:58:42.434130       1 nodemanager.go:395] node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
E0404 14:58:42.434133       1 vsphere.go:651] Cannot find node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" in cache. Node not found!!!
I0404 14:58:42.434138       1 vsphere.go:1020] Node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" does not exist, disk [WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk is already detached from node.
I0404 14:58:42.434160       1 operation_generator.go:513] DetachVolume.Detach succeeded for volume "nil" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") on node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" 
```

The in-tree cloud provider has a [node informer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/vsphere.go#L1547) and [maintains a list of nodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d89d5ab2680bc74fe4487ad71e514f4e0812d9ce/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/nodemanager.go#L290) from it. It apparently has not processed all nodes at the time A/D controller tries to detach the node.

### What did you expect to happen?

The in-tree vSphere volume plugin + cloud provider detaches the volume in vCenter.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

That's really tricky, it's very hard / impossible to reproduce on a real cluster. I had to inject errors to Detach() in-tree volume call, so they fail until KCM is restarted. Newly started KCM would detach the volume just fine (no error would be injected there), but marks the volume as detached right away.

### Anything else we need to know?

For the record (and search-ability), the CSI driver that tries to attach the volume to another node complains either:

```
Warning  FailedAttachVolume  26m (x10 over 31m)   attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-24d840d4-89eb-4619-945d-fce26be85015" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to set keepAfterDeleteVm control flag for VolumeID "76f9905e-22ff-443d-bf8e-1af270ab5b46"
```

Or:

```
LocalizedMessage: (string) (len=32) \"The resource 'volume' is in use.\"\n})\n". opId: "1bb54dd7"
```

cc @xing-yang @jingxu97 @msau42 @gnufied @divyenpatel

It could be somewhat related to https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/vsphere-csi-driver/issues/2165, however, not all cases of https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/vsphere-csi-driver/issues/2165 can be related to KCM restart. As I mentioned above, it's very hard/impossible to synchronize KCM restart with draining a node in a real cluster.

I0404 14:58:42.423920       1 operation_generator.go:1637] Verified volume is safe to detach for volume "nil" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") on node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk"

ROOT CAUSE: The vSphere cloud provider maintains an internal cache of nodes using informer events that are asynchronous. During kube-controller-manager startup, this cache may not yet be fully populated when volume detach operations occur. This causes the volume to remain indefinitely attached in vCenter.
FIX: Fixed vSphere cloud provider not to skip detach volumes from nodes at kube-controller-startup.

Reflector retains initial list result for a long time
### What happened?

The result of initial list in Reflector is kept in the memory until the last element in the items list hasn't been changed. 

In practice this can be a long time, e.g. there can be some stable pod that are running for days, in configmaps there is a kube-root-ca.crt which stays there forever.

This problem is described here: https://go.dev/blog/slices-intro#a-possible-gotcha

IIUC this affects both:
* clients using informers/Reflectors
* kube-apiserver which is using the same Reflector to initialize watch cache

This means e.g. when all (but 1) elements are frequently updated, the memory usage is 2x the state size (the initial size + current size).

### What did you expect to happen?

When the objects are deleted from the cluster, the memory consumption of the Reflector drops.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Create cluster with 1GB state of significant size (e.g. by creating 1000 configmaps of size 1M each)
* Start informer (e.g. I was using https://gist.github.com/mborsz/8964c84b298ee63c7153190d608a7464)
* Observe memory usage (it should be around ~1GB as expected)
  * Sample [pprof](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/197553760-cfd8a8f0-0996-4ee7-8f8c-5ea72e06bf8d.png)
* Remove 99% of the state
* [issue] Observe memory usage (it stays around ~1GB, despite state taking ~10M)
  * Sample [pprof](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/197555163-adff7e50-e0db-4c75-8397-929b08dc9c08.png)
* Recreate the state (with the same name)
* [issue] The memory usage grows to ~2G
  * Sample [pprof](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/197557325-f3aef1f3-c003-4f17-83db-5aac06ab5643.png)


### Anything else we need to know?

This seems to be consequence of the:
* ConfigMapList using []ConfigMap type (not []*ConfigMap)
* Reflector taking pointer to those objects https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fe9d04763b94366a7a80a1ef3d9f83337eac722e/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/meta/help.go#L195-L200
* If any of the elements is in use, the entire Items is kept in the memory.

The naive fix would be to create a DeepCopy before storing data in Reflector, but this requires careful implementation to avoid increasing memory usage at the beginning (as we can easily have a list in Items and a deep copied list at the same time).

1.26

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The result of initial list in Reflector is kept in the memory until the last element in the items list hasn't been changed.

* clients using informers/Reflectors
* kube-apiserver which is using the same Reflector to initialize watch cache

This means e.g. when all (but 1) elements are frequently updated, the memory usage is 2x the state size (the initial size + current size).

### What did you expect to happen?

When the objects are deleted from the cluster, the memory consumption of the Reflector drops.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Create cluster with 1GB state of significant size (e.g. by creating 1000 configmaps of size 1M each)
* Start informer (e.g. I was using https://gist.github.com/mborsz/8964c84b298ee63c7153190d608a7464)
* Observe memory usage (it should be around ~1GB as expected)
  * Sample [pprof](https://user-i
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that the initial list result in the Reflector retains references to a large slice of objects, and if any object pointer from that slice is still in use, the Go runtime keeps the entire backing array in memory. This happens because the ObjectList contains a slice of objects (not pointers), and the Reflector takes pointers to these objects, preventing garbage collection of the initial slice. client-go prints a klog warning by default in library code which is not allowed
**What happened**:

A code change was merged that used `klog.Warningf` in library code by default (`NewDefaultClientLoadingRules` changed in a way that impacted all code in the world which uses that default, which is pretty common), which is not allowed by convention in Kube because client libraries may be used in UIs that wish to control output (klog is not consistent with other output).  The code change should have had a callback that allowed clients to optionally decide to print, not print to Warningf by default.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/78185#issuecomment-685765692

We should also document the convention for other reviewers that logging by default in client libraries is disallowed.

For instance, a callback would have allowed kubectl to print a human readable message `warning: KUBECONFIG does not exist` in general, and in specific cases (like `kubectl config` or login flows where KUBECONFIG not existing is totally reasonable) not print a message.

wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true does not invoke condition function at least once
### What happened?

Calling wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true does not invoke the passed condition function if context has already been cancelled.


### What did you expect to happen?

wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true should invoke the passed condition function at least once even if context has already been cancelled as wait.PollUntilContextCancel documentation says:

> If immediate is true, condition will be invoked before waiting and guarantees that condition is invoked at least once, regardless of whether the context has been cancelled.

Note that wait.PollUntilContextTimeout wraps wait.PollUntilContextCancel, so the above should be applied to wait.PollUntilContextTimeout as well.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```go
package main

import (
        "context"
        "time"

        "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait"
)

func main() {
        err := wait.PollUntilContextTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second, 0, true, func(context.Context) (bool, error) {
                return true, nil
        })
        if err != nil {
                panic(err)
        }
}

TITLE: wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true does not invoke condition function at least once
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Calling wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true does not invoke the passed condition function if context has already been cancelled.


### What did you expect to happen?

wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true should invoke the passed condition function at least once even if context has already been cancelled as wait.PollUntilContextCancel documentation says:

> If immediate is true, condition will be invoked before waiting and guarantees that condition is invoked at least once, regardless of whether the context has been cancelled.

Note that wait.PollUntilContextTimeout wraps wait.PollUntilContextCancel, so the above should be applied to wait.PollUntilContextTimeout as well.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```go
package main

import (
        "context"
        "time"

        "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait"
)

func main() {
        err := wait.PollUntilContextTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second, 0, true, func(context.Context) (bool, error) {
                return true, nil
        })
        if err != nil {
                panic(err)
        }
}
```

This program pan
ROOT CAUSE: The implementation of wait.PollUntilContextTimeout immediately checks the context for cancellation before executing the condition function. This causes the condition function to never be called if the context is already cancelled, violating the API contract that the condition must be called at least once when immediate=true.
FIX: wait.PollUntilContextTimeout function, if immediate is true, the condition will be invoked before waiting and guarantees that the condition is invoked at least once, regardless of whether the context has been cancelled.
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/loop.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/loop_test.go

Indexed Jobs can break with high number of parallelism or completions
### What happened?

Currently, the maximum number of completions is MAX_INT32, around 2e9 and the maximum parallelism is 1e5.

When using these values, and assuming a very unlucky case, the field `.status.completedIndexes` can fill up the maximum size for objects in etcd (around 1.5Mi)


### What did you expect to happen?

An Indexed Job with the maximum number of completions and parallelism to be correctly tracked.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: sample-job
spec:
  completionMode: Indexed
  completions: 2000000000
  parallelism: 100000
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: bad
        image: python
        command:
        - python3
        - -c
        - |
          import os
          import time
          id = int(os.environ.get("JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX"))
          if id > 1000000000 and id % 3 == 0:
            time.sleep(10000)
      restartPolicy: Never
```

In other words, every index multiple of 3 takes too long to terminate.

### Anything else we need to know?

In the example above, the number of characters needed by the `completedIndexes` field is:

`(10+1)*2*1e5`, roughly 2Mi, where:
- 10 is the number of characters for a number
- 1 for the separating character.
- 2 for the consecutive numbers
- 1e5 for the number of "holes" in the `completedIndexes`, based on the parallelism.

### Kubernetes version

1.21 and newer (when IndexedJob was introduced)

any

kubelet: PreStop Hooks can hang termination of a pod beyond pod's termination grace period
### What happened?

Termination grace period includes the termination time of prestop hooks and containers in the pod. The total time that the pod terminates should always be < termination grace period seconds.

A misconfigured pod with a preStopHook that hangs indefinitely and pod ignoring SIGTERM can result in the pod taking 2X (double) the termination grace period seconds to terminate.
 

### What did you expect to happen?

The time to terminate the pod should always be <= termination grace period seconds including prestop hook execution time as documented in https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/#hook-handler-execution

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1) Apply the following pod

```
kind: Pod
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: prestop-repro
  labels:
    pod: prestop-repro
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
  containers:
  - name: busybox
    lifecycle:
      preStop:
        exec:
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 999999"]
    image: k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images/nginx:1.14-2
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
    args:
      - |
        _term() {
            echo "Caught SIGTERM signal!"
            while true; do sleep 5; done
        }
        trap _term SIGTERM
        while true; do sleep 5; done
```

```

kube-proxy in LocalModeNodeCIDR mode may cache stale Node.PodCIDR if the Node object is recreated
### What happened?

If `LocalModeNodeCIDR` is true, kube-proxy reads the `Node.PodCIDR` value and uses it to determine whether or not traffic is local to the Node.

In certain cases (e.g. when kube-proxy runs before the Node information has been completely updated), it is possible for kube-proxy to read and store a stale `PodCIDR` value. This will cause kube-proxy to route traffic incorrectly as the local traffic determination is no longer correct.

Note: PodCIDR is immutable once set but it is possible to delete and recreate the Node object to get into this state. (yes, this can happen)



### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy should detect this state and reconfigure/restart with the newly updated `PodCIDR`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Recreate the Node object with a different PodCIDR after kube-proxy has started on the Node.

### Kubernetes version

Impacts all current versions that support `LocalModeNodeCIDR`

### Cloud provider

<details>
Observed for GCE preemptible/spot VMs, but is a generic problem.
</details>

Note: PodCIDR is immutable once set but it is possible to delete and recreate the Node object to get into this state. (yes, this can happen)

<details>

ROOT CAUSE: kube-proxy reads the Node object's PodCIDR at startup and caches it, but does not update this cached PodCIDR when the Node object is deleted and recreated with a different PodCIDR. Therefore, kube-proxy continues to use the stale PodCIDR for local traffic determination, causing incorrect routing.
FIX: kube-proxy, will restart in case it detects that the Node assigned pod.Spec.PodCIDRs have changed

imagePullSecrets should log warning if secret does not exist
#### What happened:

imagePullSecrets can added to a pod manifest to reference a secret containing registry credentials. Currently, if you add the name of a secret that does not exist, there is no warning or error. 

#### What you expected to happen:

I would expect there to be an error and a failed deployment if the secret does not exist/cannot be found in the namespace. 
If people are pulling public images, they may still wish to authenticate to a registry, for example dockerhub, before pulling the image, in order to utilise their subscription account rate limits. Currently if they use imagePullSecrets and the referenced secret does not exist, they may assume they are authenticating to their account when they are not, and will still be able to pull public images without any warning that authentication is not taking place. 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Add `imagePullSecrets: myfakesecret` to a pod spec, and pull images from docker.io.

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

In KubeVirt project, we now see a regression when running on Kubernetes `1.25.10 | 1.26.5 | 1.27.2`. If kubelet is restarted on a node, then all the existing and running workloads that use devices are terminated with `UnexpectedAdmissionError`:
```
Warning  UnexpectedAdmissionError  45s   kubelet            Allocate failed due to no healthy devices present; cannot allocate unhealthy devices devices.kubevirt.io/kvm, which is unexpected
Normal   Killing                   42s   kubelet            Stopping container compute
```
KubeVirt runs virtual machines inside pods and uses a device plugin to advertise e.g. `/dev/kvm` on the nodes.

Presumably, this PR changed the behavior: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116376
Original issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109595

kubelet (1.27.1) fails to mount a hostPath volume for a static pod
### What happened?

This is a bit hard to reproduce, as it happens in a very specific setup, the problems only happens with `kubelet` 1.27.1, downgrading to 1.26.4 fixes the problem.

In a single-node cluster controlplane pods run as static pods, Rook/Ceph is deployed, and some PVs/PVCs backed by Ceph.

After a unclean shutdown related to some PVs backed by Ceph not being unmounted (this is not a Kubernetes), the `kubelet` which comes up after a reboot doesn't start controlplane static pods, which essentially blocks every other pod from starting (as API server is done).

After a reboot, kubelet is running, but it keeps reporting an error about static pods like:

```
172.20.0.2: {"ts":1683110056228.5916,"caller":"kubelet/kubelet.go:1875","msg":"Unable to attach or mount volumes for pod; skipping pod","pod":{"name":"kube-apiserver-talos-default-controlplane-1","namespace":"kube-system"},"err":"unmounted volumes=[audit secrets config], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition"}
```

All of the volumes are `hostPath` volumes in a static pod:

```yaml
        volumes:
            - hostPath:
                path: /system/secrets/kubernetes/kube-apiserver
              name: secrets
            - hostPath:
                path: /system/config/kubernetes/kube-apiserver
              name: config
            - hostPath:
                path: /var/log/audit/kube
              name: audit
```

The kubelet is stuck in this state "forever", I tested at least for 8 hours.

If I downgrade the kubelet (without machine reboot) to 1.26.4, it immediately starts the static pods bringing up the node online.

If I try same scenario with reboot with kubelet 1.26.4, the problem doesn't occur either.


### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should run static pods after a reboot.

TITLE: kubelet (1.27.1) fails to mount a hostPath volume for a static pod
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

This is a bit hard to reproduce, as it happens in a very specific setup, the problems only happens with `kubelet` 1.27.1, downgrading to 1.26.4 fixes the problem.

In a single-node cluster controlplane pods run as static pods, Rook/Ceph is deployed, and some PVs/PVCs backed by Ceph.

After a unclean shutdown related to some PVs backed by Ceph not being unmounted (this is not a Kubernetes), the `kubelet` which comes up after a reboot doesn't start controlplane static pods, which essentially blocks every other pod from starting (as API server is done).

After a reboot, kubelet is running, but it keeps reporting an error about static pods like:

```
172.20.0.2: {"ts":1683110056228.5916,"caller":"kubelet/kubelet.go:1875","msg":"Unable to attach or mount volumes for pod; skipping pod","pod":{"name":"kube-apiserver-talos-default-controlplane-1","namespace":"kube-system"},"err":"unmounted volumes=[audit secrets config], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition"}
```

All of the volumes are `hostPath` volumes in a static pod:

```yaml
        volumes:
            - hostPath:
                path: /system/s
ROOT CAUSE: The bug was caused by the kubelet's volume reconstruction logic incorrectly relying on the availability of the CSIDriver API objects to determine if a volume is attachable during startup. When the kubelet started, it sometimes lacked connection to the API server and thus could not query the CSIDriver, causing the CSI volume reconstruction to hang and prevent static pods with volumes from starting. The code assumed API server availability that might not exist during early kubelet startup, leading to indefinite waits for volume conditions.
FIX: Fixed kubelet startup getting stuck with `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature enabled and a CSI volume present in /var/lib/kubelet/pods.
FILES: pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/cache/actual_state_of_world.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/cache/actual_state_of_world_test.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_new.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_new_test.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_common.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_new.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_new_test.go

Mismatched URLs for service-account-issuer-discovery and Open API Spec's swagger.json
### What happened?

When I use the official Kubernetes Java Client (version 18.0.0) from within a pod using `Config.defaultClient()` to build an `ApiClient` and then access `getServiceAccountIssuerOpenIDConfiguration` in the `WellKnownApi` I get the following error:

```json
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:test:user\" cannot get path \"/.well-known/openid-configuration/\"",
  "reason": "Forbidden",
  "details": {},
  "code": 403
}
```

The same happens with the `OpenidApi#getServiceAccountIssuerOpenIDKeyset`.

However, the problem does not happen when I call the `/.well-known/openid-configuration` endpoint using the pod's service account and curl.

The problem is that the generated Open API spec indicates that the client should call `/.well-known/openid-configuration/` instead of `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (and similarly `/openid/v1/jwks/` instead of `/openid/v1/jwks`). While the API Server seems to resolve these endpoints just fine, the `ClusterRole` defined in the code does not have the trailing slashes and therefore rejects the requests with a 403:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6a75e7c40cab5a0d96d815c3aa976dc98b4b0972/plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/bootstrappolicy/policy.go#L521-L530

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected to be able to access these APIs from within a pod that has a mounted service account because this [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#service-account-issuer-discovery) suggests all that is required is a service account and because all clusters get this `ClusterRoleBinding` and this `ClusterRole` by default:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  annotations:
    rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate: "true"
  labels:
    kubernetes.io/bootstrapping: rbac-defaults
  name: system:service-account-issuer-discovery
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: system:service-account-issuer-discovery
subjects:
- apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Group
  name: system:serviceaccounts
```

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  annotations:
    rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate: "true"
  labels:
    kubernetes.io/bootstrapping: rbac-defaults
  name: system:service-account-issuer-discovery
rules:
- nonResourceURLs:
  - /.well-known/openid-configuration
  - /openid/v1/jwks
  verbs:
  - get
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Here is the Java snippet to reproduce it:

```Java
        ApiClient k8sApiClient = Config.fromCluster();
        WellKnownApi wellKnownApi = new WellKnownApi(k8sApiClient);
        try {
            wellKnownApi.getServiceAccountIssuerOpenIDConfiguration();
        } catch (ApiException e) {
            LOG.error("Message: " + e.getMessage() + " Response body: " + e.getResponseBody());
        }
```

When run from within a pod that has a service account mounted into it, the above code will fail.

You can also reproduce the error without the Java Client by running `curl --cacert /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)"  https://kubernetes.default.svc/.well-known/openid-configuration/` from within a pod.

I can resolve the issue by updating the `system:service-account-issuer-discovery` cluster role to have the endpoints with the trailing `/`.

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  annotations:
    rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate: "true"
  labels:
    kubernetes.io/bootstrapping: rbac-defaults
  name: system:service-account-issuer-discovery
rules:
- nonResourceURLs:
  - /.well-known/openid-configuration/
  - /.well-known/openid-configuration
  - /openid/v1/jwks/
  - /openid/v1/jwks
  verbs:
  - get
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I am happy to provide a fix, if I can get the right pointers. The detail I'm unclear on is how to fix this in a backwards compatible way.

Also, this PR seems to have introduced the potentially problematic `swagger.json` entry: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93258.

<details>

Here is one of the remote clusters I reproduced the issues with.

```console
$ kubectl version
 kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"25", GitVersion:"v1.25.3", GitCommit:"434bfd82814af038ad94d62ebe59b133fcb50506", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-10-12T10:47:25Z", GoVersion:"go1.19.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}

WARNING: version difference between client (1.25) and server (1.23) exceeds the supported minor version skew of +/-1
```

### Cloud provider

I reproduced this bug in multiple cloud providers as well as in minikube. It does not appear to be cloud provider specific.

StatefulSet with `podManagementPolicy: Parallel` should create pods in parallel
### What would you like to be added?

When `podManagementPolicy: Parallel` is set, StatefulSetController should issue create requests for replicas in batches (similar to how other controllers work, e.g. ReplicaSetController) when creating pods for the first time and scaling up.

### Why is this needed?

Currently even with `Parallel` podManagementPolicy StatefulSet the replicas are still _created_ sequentially, even though they can start to _run_ in any order.

This severely limits pod throughput when working with large StatefulSets (~thousands of replicas). For example, 10 StatefulSets with 5k pods each achieve a total of ~6 pods/s, while 1k StatefulSets with 50 pods each allows for creating ~120 pods/s. 

`Parallel` policy suggests the pods can be created sequentially (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/workload-resources/stateful-set-v1/#StatefulSetSpec): 

>The alternative policy is Parallel which will create pods in parallel to match the desired scale without waiting, and on scale down will delete all pods at once.

Relevant code (`Parallel` policy controls the value of `monotonic`): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L424)

Jobs create replacement Pods as soon as a Pod is marked for deletion
### What happened?

When a Pod belonging to a Job is deleted, the job controller creates a replacement pod immediately, even if parallelism is set to 1 and backoffLimit is set to 0.

### What did you expect to happen?

This depends on the use case, but some applications fail when there are more than one pod.

For example, tensorflow fails with:

```
 /job:worker/task:4: Duplicate task registration with task_name=/job:worker/replica:0/task:4
```

This applications will benefit from a delayed Pod creation until the original Pod is marked as Failed/Succeeded.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Job that takes some time to clean up on SIGTERM. You can use `gcr.io/k8s-staging-perf-tests/sleep` with `-termination-grace-period 1m`
2. Delete the pod.
3. Observe that there are two pods running.

While here we do a manual DELETE, it could come as a result of preemption from kube-scheduler or a Node maintenance event, which could be common.

### Anything else we need to know?

IIUC, the existing behavior is similar to that of ReplicaSets and it's the behavior that Jobs had from the beginning.

A comment from an internal discussion with @erictune:

> This non-locking behavior was chosen when Job was designed.  At that time, there was no completionMode: Indexed.  Without an index, even if we waited for complete termination, the user would still need to do their own locking/coordination process, or ensure idempotence.  So it would just slow down the Job controller with no benefit.  

Also, at that time there was no PodFailurePolicy. If the user sets a rule for FailJob, we might be creating a replacement pod before being able to act on the policy (related to point 3 in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-apps/3329-retriable-and-non-retriable-failures#marking-pods-as-failed kubernetes/enhancements#3329).

So I propose that we treat this as a bugfix for Jobs (Indexed or NonIndexed) that use the PodFailurePolicy (still in Beta).

While an argument could be made that this is an issue with Indexed Jobs, regardless of whether they are using PodFailurePolicy, it's unclear if there are users depending on fast recreation. We could provide this as an option in the PodFailurePolicy as well.

master

TITLE: `kubectl expose` fails for apps with same-port, different-protocol
SYMPTOM: Given this deployment:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: multiport
spec:
  replicas: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: multiport
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: multiport
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: k8s.gcr.io/serve_hostname:v1.4
        name: c1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 93
          protocol: TCP
        - containerPort: 93
          protocol: UDP
```

```
$ k expose deploy multiport
The Service "multiport" is invalid: spec.ports[1]: Duplicate value: core.ServicePort{Name:"", Protocol:"UDP", AppProtocol:(*string)(nil), Port:93, TargetPort:intstr.IntOrString{Type:0, IntVal:0, StrVal:""}, NodePort:0}
```

Looking at staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/expose/expose.go, it builds a `protocolsMap` which reduces those 2 ports to one protocol.  It should probably just return a list of {proto, port} or even {proto, port, name} which it extracts from the target.
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because kubectl expose internally builds a map from port numbers to protocols, collapsing multiple protocols on the same port into one entry. This logic does not support having the same port number exposed with different protocols (TCP and UDP), causing a duplicate port error when multiple protocols share a port number.

Scheduling Pods with dynamic resources and using the Pod `.spec.nodeName` field fails
### What happened?

The combination of using the Pod spec nodeName field with the `DynamicResources` scheduler plugin (currently feature-gated) doesn't work. No surprise really as the nodeName field effective bypasses the `DynamicResources` scheduler plugin running, and something rather clever would need to be invented to make things to work. But this is still a bit of a regression compared to the old device plugin model which doesn't have a similar limitation.  @pohly as the author of the dynamic resources feature can explain what could maybe be created to fix this.

Granted, forcing scheduling even with a device plugin resource may or may not succeed at the node level depending on the availability of said plugin resources at the node, but with dynamic resources the failure seems to be currently guaranteed.

The use-case for this is such that the Kubernetes scheduler is effectively being preceded by some other scheduler which runs earlier (say, some HPC framework) which is giving the Pods the node names and somehow knows that there will be enough resources, and then the workloads ought to land in the specified node and the container related work is then handled normally from there on. So basically Kubernetes wouldn't do much in terms of scheduling, but takes over from there.

### What did you expect to happen?

TBH I expected it to fail and it did. The resource claims won't work, since the scheduler plugin isn't getting a chance to do its thing.

the preemption happens even when PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable 
When PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable, we don't need to run the preemption, but currently we run.
This unexpected preemption could cause errors from the preemption by trying to read non-exist PreFilter data.

As @Huang-Wei pointed out ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119770#issuecomment-1666418637)), actually we didn't run the preemption in such cases in the past versions, but https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110894 introduced this bug.

SYMPTOM: When PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable, we don't need to run the preemption, but currently we run.

As @Huang-Wei pointed out ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119770#issuecomment-1666418637)), actually we didn't run the preemption in such cases in the past versions, but https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110894 introduced this bug.
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because the scheduler's preemption logic was executed even when the PreFilter phase indicated the pod was unschedulable and unresolvable, a scenario where preemption should be skipped. This behavior was changed unintentionally by a prior PR, causing preemption to run and attempt to access prefilter data that does not exist, resulting in errors.
FIX: Fixed a 1.26 regression scheduling bug by ensuring that preemption is skipped when a PreFilter plugin returns `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`

CronJob gets stuck when jobs quota is reached
### What happened?

We (in Booking.com) run CronJobs in Kubernetes clusters with ResourceQuota's defined. When quota for # of jobs is reached we observed that CronJobs:
1. stop scheduling new jobs (because quota is reached),
2. don't clean the old jobs (despite # of jobs > history allows and the fact that it would unblock the CronJob new Jobs). 

The only way to progress is to remove enough Jobs to make room for a new Job in namespace quota. When we do that manually, the CronJob kicks in.

The workaround we found around the internet is to specify `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for the job template. But it's not ideal as it's not a history-based limit, but a time-based limit, and often you want to have the last N jobs to be around for debugging.

### What did you expect to happen?

When jobs quota is reached and # of cronjob jobs exceeds specified the history limit, these jobs are deleted giving room for new jobs to run.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: job-quota
  namespace: default
spec:
  hard:
    count/jobs.batch: "1"
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cronjob
spec:
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 0
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: hello-world
              image: bash
              command: ["bash", "-c", "sleep 80"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

1. Wait for a first Job to be created (which will fill up the jobs quota) at X minute.
2. A job for X + 1 will fail to be created (because quota won't allow, and X job is still running).
3. All future attempts to create a new job by the controller will fail (check `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail`, you'll see re-occuring `Error creating job: jobs.batch "hello-world-cronjob-28187648" is forbidden: exceeded quota: job-quota, requested: count/jobs.batch=1, used: count/jobs.batch=1, limited: count/jobs.batch=1`).
4. The first job will never be cleaned (although it will be eligible, since history is 0).

### Anything else we need to know?

Looks like the problem was introduced in the `cronjob_controllerv2.go` implementation: if `jm.syncCronJob` returned an error, we return from the function and never invoke `jm.cleanupFinishedJobs`.:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L199-L213

In the old `cronjob_controller.go` implementation this was not the case:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f77da5bd4809927e15d1658fb4aa8f13ad890a5/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controller.go#L137-L138

sched: CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins not always injected into cycleState
### What happened?

In k8s 1.27, scheduler introduced a new "short circuit" semantics in PreFilter to bypass a Pod quickly. A change introduced here is it relies on that plugin to be stored in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins`, which makes sense as what it was explained [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125/files#r1062646736).

However, the `SkipFilterPlugins` info, although is populated upon each plugin's PreFilter invocation, is not injected into `CycleState` when some PreFilter returns unschedulable:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L655-L661

So think about this workflow:

- pluginA returns Skip in its PreFilter
- pluginB return Unschedulable in its PreFilter

TITLE: sched: CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins not always injected into cycleState
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

In k8s 1.27, scheduler introduced a new "short circuit" semantics in PreFilter to bypass a Pod quickly. A change introduced here is it relies on that plugin to be stored in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins`, which makes sense as what it was explained [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125/files#r1062646736).

However, the `SkipFilterPlugins` info, although is populated upon each plugin's PreFilter invocation, is not injected into `CycleState` when some PreFilter returns unschedulable:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L655-L661

So think about this workflow:

- pluginA returns Skip in its PreFilter
- pluginB return Unschedulable in its PreFilter
- note: pluginA is not included in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` due to aforementioned bug
- a Pod is claimed as unschedulable (failed by pluginB)
- during PostFilter, it's **supposed** to bypass pluginA's PreEnqueueExtension's AddPod/RemovePod, but it doesn't
- calling a "skipped" Plugin's AddPod/RemovePod during preemption, sometimes will abort the whole preemption as the logic tries to rea
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because the scheduler framework did not properly inject the SkipFilterPlugins information into the CycleState when a PreFilter plugin returned Unschedulable. As a result, during PostFilter, plugins that relied on CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins to know which plugins to skip could fail or behave incorrectly because this information was missing.
FIX: Fixed a 1.27 scheduling regression that PostFilter plugin may not function if previous PreFilter plugins return Skip
FILES: pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go, pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework_test.go, test/integration/scheduler/preemption/preemption_test.go

CEL Estimated cost incorrect for lowerAscii
### What happened?

Creating a CRD with a case-insensitive uniqueness check and appropriate maxLength/maxItems limits should be allowed:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: uniquetests.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                headers:
                  type: array
                  maxItems: 1
                  x-kubernetes-validations:
                    - rule: "self.all(item1, self.exists_one(item2, item1.name.lowerAscii() == item2.name.lowerAscii()))"
                  items:
                    type: object
                    properties:
                      name:
                        maxLength: 1
                        type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: uniquetests
    singular: uniquetest
    kind: UniqueTest
```

But I got:

```
kubectl apply -f unique.yaml
The CustomResourceDefinition "uniquetests.stable.example.com" is invalid: 
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[headers].x-kubernetes-validations[0].rule: Forbidden: estimated rule cost exceeds budget by factor of more than 100x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared)
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[headers].x-kubernetes-validations[0].rule: Forbidden: contributed to estimated rule cost total exceeding cost limit for entire OpenAPIv3 schema
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema: Forbidden: x-kubernetes-validations estimated rule cost total for entire OpenAPIv3 schema exceeds budget by factor of more than 100x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared)
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the estimated cost to be very low with maxItems=1 and maxLength=1.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This also exceeds the estimated cost limit, suggesting the problem is unrelated to the array:

```yaml
 x-kubernetes-validations:                                                                                        
  - rule: "self[0].name.lowerAscii() == self[0].name.lowerAscii()"
```

But this is valid (estimated cost is under the limit):

```yaml
x-kubernetes-validations:                                                                                        
  - rule: "self.all(item1, self.exists_one(item2, item1.name == item2.name))"
```

Which suggests that the estimated cost system is not handling `lowerAscii` correctly.  The estimated cost of `lowerAscii` should be a function of the input string length (which in this case has a max length of 1), and, for purposes of subsequent cost calculations, the resulting value of `lowerAscii` should be known by the estimated cost system to be the same length as the input string.



### Anything else we need to know?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/library/cost.go#L119 is where the estimated cost of lowerAscii is handled. Just glancing at the code I don't see an obvious problem.

ROOT CAUSE: The root cause was that the estimated cost calculation for CEL functions returning strings, bytes, lists, or maps did not correctly propagate the size of their result values. ### What happened?

`PodDisruptionBudget` with an empty selector `{}` selects all the pods as expected.
But, during the `drain` /`eviction`, the pdb is not being honored correctly i.e. all the pods are getting evicted.

This issue is only observed with the empty selector and works as expected if a valid label selector is provided that selects all the pods in a namespace.

### What did you expect to happen?

When an empty selector `{}` is provided in the `PodDisruptionBudget`'s spec, the created `PodDisruptionBudget` needs to be honored by not evicting all the pods during the `drain/eviction` api call

  labels:
    app: busybox
  name: busybox
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busybox
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busybox
    spec:

Service `status.loadBalancer.ingress` can be set when `type` != `LoadBalancer`
xref 119454

I think this may be one of the few cases where we can actually change the behavior in a "breaking" way.

User creates service with `.type=ClusterIP`, `.status.loadBalancer` is empty
Controller or user updates the status subresource, sets `.spec.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip` (not wiped or validated, should be)
User updates `service spec` in any way, `.staus.loadBalancer` is wiped

It's clear that the `.status.loadBalancer` is not meant to be set when `.type` is not "LoadBalancer".

The question is:

1) Fail validation?
2) Silently discard the value?
3) Warn and then discard the value?
4) Just warn and leave it.

Because we allowed it in the past, but it is so volatile, I lean towards 3.

@aojea and @khenidak - the people most familair with this type.

Edit: PrepareForUpdate() runs before warnings.  So:

(1) is easy
(2) is easy
(4) is slightly less easy than (2)
(3) is slightly less easy than (4)

TITLE: Service `status.loadBalancer.ingress` can be set when `type` != `LoadBalancer`
SYMPTOM: xref 119454

I think this may be one of the few cases where we can actually change the behavior in a "breaking" way.

User creates service with `.type=ClusterIP`, `.status.loadBalancer` is empty
Controller or user updates the status subresource, sets `.spec.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip` (not wiped or validated, should be)
User updates `service spec` in any way, `.staus.loadBalancer` is wiped

It's clear that the `.status.loadBalancer` is not meant to be set when `.type` is not "LoadBalancer".

The question is:

1) Fail validation?
2) Silently discard the value?
3) Warn and then discard the value?
4) Just warn and leave it.

Because we allowed it in the past, but it is so volatile, I lean towards 3.

@aojea and @khenidak - the people most familair with this type.

Edit: PrepareForUpdate() runs before warnings.  So:

(1) is easy
(2) is easy
(4) is slightly less easy than (2)
(3) is slightly less easy than (4)
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that the system allowed setting the Service's .status.loadBalancer field even when the Service's .spec.type was not "LoadBalancer". This created inconsistent state because any spec update would clear the ingress status, making it unreliable to have loadBalancer status on non-LoadBalancer services. The lack of validation permitted invalid state to be stored temporarily, leading to confusion and volatility in the status value.
FIX: Setting the `status.loadBalancer` of a Service whose `spec.type` is not `"LoadBalancer"` was previously allowed, but any update to the `metadata` or `spec` would wipe that field. Setting this field is no longer permitted unless `spec.type` is  `"LoadBalancer"`.  In the very unlikely event that this has unexpected impact, you can enable the `AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB` feature gate, which will restore the previous behavior.  If you do need to set this, please file an issue with the Kubernetes project to help contributors understand why you need it.
FILES: pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go, pkg/apis/core/validation/validation_test.go, pkg/features/kube_features.go, pkg/registry/core/service/strategy_test.go, test/integration/apiserver/apply/reset_fields_test.go, test/integration/etcd/data.go

Namespace stuck in Terminating when deleted if ApiService doesn't implement Aggregated Discovery
### What happened?

We implement a manual `APIService` API Extension in [Agones](https://github.com/googleforgames/agones).

Definition:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/install/helm/agones/templates/service/allocation.yaml

Code for handling web requests:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go

The code is extremely lightweight as we only have no need for storage, and only accept CREATE requests at this time.

This issue was first reported by one of our users in May, but we only were able to reproduce it ourselves once we were on 1.27.x: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172

Testing on Kubernetes 1.27.x we noticed that when attempting to delete Namespaces, they would get stuck in termination with the following description:

```
❯ kubectl describe ns 1690585578
Name:         1690585578
Labels:       kubernetes.io/metadata.name=1690585578
              owner=e2e-test
Annotations:  <none>
Status:       Terminating
Conditions:
  Type                                         Status  LastTransitionTime               Reason                  Message
  ----                                         ------  ------------------               ------                  -------
  NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure            True    Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:44 -0700  DiscoveryFailed         Discovery failed for some groups, 1 failing: unable to retrieve the complete list of server APIs: allocation.agones.dev/v1: stale GroupVersion discovery: allocation.agones.dev/v1
  NamespaceDeletionGroupVersionParsingFailure  False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:46 -0700  ParsedGroupVersions     All legacy kube types successfully parsed
  NamespaceDeletionContentFailure              False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentDeleted          All content successfully deleted, may be waiting on finalization
  NamespaceContentRemaining                    False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentRemoved          All content successfully removed
  NamespaceFinalizersRemaining                 False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentHasNoFinalizers  All content-preserving finalizers finished
```

So far, I've not found a way to delete the Namespace.

Looking through the log for the webserver, i can see requests for `/apis` and the new Aggregated Discovery feature (`Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"`), but we return a 404 to that response, since it's not implemented.

Looking through the code I can find (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go) it seems that any response other than `http.StatusOK` would result in this issue -- which is breaking backward compatibility within `APIService` to assume that this API surface is implemented in some way.

### What did you expect to happen?

Namespaces would terminate as per normal.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install Agones on a cluster (https://agones.dev/site/docs/installation/install-agones/)
2. `kubectl create ns foo`
3. `kubectl delete ns foo`
4. Watch as the ns gets stuck in Terminating.


### Anything else we need to know?

If I had a magic wand, I'd love a reference of all the API's that get called against an APIService and what their expected results should be.

So far it's a combo of using `kubectl proxy` and looking at the k8s API responses, crawling through code, and reading apiserver logs to try and reverse engineer this work.

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

We implement a manual `APIService` API Extension in [Agones](https://github.com/googleforgames/agones).

Definition:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/install/helm/agones/templates/service/allocation.yaml

Code for handling web requests:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go

The code is extremely lightweight as we only have no need for storage, and only accept CREATE requests at this time.

This issue was first reported by one of our users in May, but we only were able to reproduce it ourselves once we were on 1.27.x: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172

Testing on Kubernetes 1.27.x we noticed that when attempting to delete Namespaces, they would get stuck in termination with the following description:

```
❯ kubectl describe ns 1690585578
Name:         1690585578
Labels:       kubernetes.io/metadata.name=1690585578
              owner=e2e-test
Annotations:  <none>
Status:       Terminating
Conditions:
  Type                                         Status  LastTransitionTime               Reason                  Message
  ----                                   
ROOT CAUSE: The Aggregated Discovery feature introduced in Kubernetes 1.27 assumed that aggregated API servers implement and respond properly to new discovery requests with specific Accept headers. If they don't implement this feature and respond with non-200 status or do not provide the expected content-type, the kube-apiserver fails to fallback to legacy discovery, causing namespace deletions to stall due to discovery failures.
FIX: Fixed a regression in default 1.27 configurations in kube-apiserver: fixed the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature (beta in 1.27+) to successfully fetch discovery information from aggregated API servers that do not check `Accept` headers when serving the `/apis` endpoint

api: Finalizer name format is not enforced for custom resources
### What happened?

A client is allowed to add custom finalizers to Custom Resources with a finalizer name that's not fully qualified (e.g. `example` or `example.com`).

However they're prevented from doing the same on builtin resource types, returning the following error:

    Invalid value: "finalizers.compute.linkedin.com": name is neither a standard finalizer name nor is it fully qualified

### What did you expect to happen?

Per [Custom Resource Definition docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#finalizers:~:text=Identifiers%20of%20custom%20finalizers%20consist%20of%20a%20domain%20name%2C%20a%20forward%20slash%20and%20the%20name%20of%20the%20finalizer), custom finalizer names are expected to be in format "consist of a domain name, a forward slash and the name of the finalizer" (e.g. `foo.bar/name`).

Therefore, I expected the enforcement to be the same for CRs and builtin types.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. have a custom resource on the cluster
2. `kubectl edit` it to add `finalizers: [example.com]`
3. observe the edit does not fail
4. do the same on a builtin resource (e.g. Namespace or Pod), observe it fails

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

Reproducible at least starting from 1.21 and still on latest versions.

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The same ResourceRequirements struct is used in two only loosely related entities (Container and PersistentVolumeClaim). Extending ResourceRequirements for dynamic resource requirement had the unintended effect that the new `Claims` field also became available in a PersistentVolumeClaim.



### What did you expect to happen?

Extending one should not affect the other.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111023#pullrequestreview-1302112278:

> We just ran across this while reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107776
>
> The ResourceRequirements type is also used within the PersistentVolumeSpec type (which is also used indirectly in pod specs via ephemeral volumes), and the "clear if feature-gate is disabled" logic is only wired to podspec-handling. That means in 1.26 PVC objects or PodSpecs with ephemeral volumes defined can persist data in this field even if the feature is disabled.
>
> Can you open a PR to clear this field in PVC and ephemeral volume create/update flows, and file a follow-up issue to consider splitting the type used in PVCs so it doesn't continue inheriting work done that is targeted at pods?

TOD
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that the API design used the same ResourceRequirements struct for both Container and PersistentVolumeClaim entities. When the struct was extended to include a new Claims field for dynamic resource requirements targeting containers, this change also inadvertently affected PersistentVolumeClaim API, where the field was not applicable. This happened because the types were shared rather than having distinct resource requirement types for containers and volume claims, causing cross-impact due to type reuse.
FIX: Go API: the ResourceRequirements struct needs to be replaced with VolumeResourceRequirements for use with volumes.
